title: Uber Driver with Electric Vehicle Needed for App Testing (France)
description:
Hi there! We are Testlio , a global software testing company with its own freelance network. Our freelancers test apps from companies across the globe. Testlio is a great place for people who value the freedom and flexibility of remote work.

At the moment, we're working with Uber to test new EV charging scenarios within the Uber Driver app — a feature currently being rolled out gradually. We're looking for already registered and active Uber drivers in France who drive an Electric Vehicle to help us ensure this feature works as expected in your region. Your feedback will be valuable in ensuring other drivers have a smooth experience using this new functionality.

Device Requirements: 

- iPhone running iOS 26 or above (tablets and iPads are not allowed)

To participate in this project, you will need to create an account on our platform. Through this account, we can assign you testing tasks. You will be asked to use our website for defect tracking and will receive materials to prepare you for testing.

Payrate: $27 USD/hr

- You will be paid per hour, not per issue/bug you find. That way, you get paid even if you don't find any bugs.

- We will reimburse you for any amount spent at charging stations while completing the testing scenarios.

- You can choose to be paid via PayPal or Payoneer for tasks completed on our website.

Benefits of being a freelancer at Testlio 

- Schedule : You can create your own schedule and work on other testing runs that interest you.

- Location : Testlio is a 100% remote company. You can work from anywhere.

- Growth : You'll be testing global-scale mobile apps and have the chance to boost your skills and grow your career.

- Payment : You are paid by the hour, not by the bug.

Requirements 

- Age : At least 18 years old.

- Location : Must be physically located anywhere in France.

- You must be an existing, active Uber driver. 

- You must own/drive an Electric Vehicle. 

- Availability : Up to 10 hours total — testing may happen across multiple days, not all in one sitting.

- Cadence : One-time project.

What does testing look like? 

- Type of testing: Functional testing of EV charging scenarios within the Uber app.

- Type of work: Short-term, freelance.

- Pay rate: $27 USD/hr.

- Payment: Paid via PayPal or Payoneer. We'll send the USD amount, which you can convert to EUR if more convenient.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Containers
description:
Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk. 

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake. 

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

Who we are 

Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk.

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

The role, in a nutshell 

Chainguard Containers is our core product, and this team builds it. As a Staff Software Engineer in Container Product Engineering you will design and ship the features, services, and build systems behind Chainguard Containers, and you will lead the small sub-teams of two to four engineers that own them.

Chainguard is growing explosively. Every line of code is now written with AI in the loop, which means the foundation it runs on has to be secure by default. You will build that foundation: the hardened container images, the registry that serves them, and the tooling that lets engineers and AI agents adopt them.

This is a product role with technical ownership. You will set direction for major new capabilities, make the architectural calls that affect the team and the teams next to it, and multiply the output of the engineers around you. You will stay hands-on: most of your week is still building.

What the team owns 

- Product features for Chainguard Containers. Letting customers push their own images to our registry, Custom Assembly (customers compose images from our hardened packages), Helm charts, notifications, and compliance views such as STIG dashboards (STIG is the US government's hardening standard).

- The image build pipeline. The systems that turn packages from Wolfi, our Linux distribution, into signed and attested container images at scale, including moving image builds onto our own runner infrastructure.

- Registry performance and distribution. Work such as lazy loading, so a container starts before its whole image has downloaded, and image signing with Sigstore.

- Adoption tooling for engineers and AI agents. Migration tools that convert existing Dockerfiles to Chainguard Containers, and MCP servers (Model Context Protocol, the standard that lets AI agents call tools) so agents can discover and pull our images directly.

What you'll do 

- Architect and drive the delivery of major new features and services for Chainguard Containers, often spanning several engineers or teams, from concept through production and the first weeks of customer use.

- Make and own the high-leverage trade-offs: which capability to build first, what to defer, when to re-platform and when not to. Write the decision down and bring dissenting engineers along.

- Work with AI coding agents as part of how you build, review, and operate, and set the standard for how the team uses them safely as volume grows.

- Follow a problem wherever it goes: into another team's service, a customer call, a support ticket, or go-to-market data, and work across team boundaries to get ahead of planning cycles.

- Mentor and level up other engineers through design review and pair work, and set the standard for how the team designs, builds, and ships.

- Partner with Product and engineering leadership on roadmap, bringing a technical point of view to what we build, not only how.

- Keep the systems you own healthy: observability, on-call, and the fixes that stop the same page from coming back.

- Write clearly and often. Design notes, decision records, and status updates are how a remote team moves fast together.

What we're looking for 

- 5+ years building and operating software that paying customers use, including leading at least one multi-engineer project end to end, preferably at a startup or a company in hyper-growth.

- High agency and urgency. You find a way, you do not wait to be unblocked, and you unblock others.

- Judgment on trade-offs at the system level. You have made calls that moved a roadmap, and you can show what you gave up and why.

- A systems thinker who designs for the whole path: build pipeline, registry, distribution, and the customer's runtime, and who sees second-order effects before they land.

- AI-native in how you build and lead. You use agentic coding tools daily and you have changed how a team works because of them.

- Comfortable with ambiguity. You can turn a half-defined product goal into a concrete technical plan, and pivot when priorities shift.

- Architectural depth in Go: you can design a Go service from scratch, not only contribute to one, plus strong API design, databases and caching, and cloud infrastructure on GCP or AWS.

- Deep knowledge of containers, container registries, the OCI image format (Open Container Initiative, the standard for container images and registries), and Kubernetes.

- A track record of mentoring engineers and raising technical practices across a team.

- Low ego. You do what you say and say what you do, and you communicate early when the news is bad.

- Excellent written English and experience working on a distributed, remote-first team.

Nice to haves 

- Software supply chain security background: SBOMs (software bill of materials), Sigstore signing, or SLSA (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts, a framework for build integrity).

- Familiarity with Chainguard's open-source tools: Wolfi, apko, and melange.

- Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code experience.

- Author of or maintainer of open-source projects.

- A non-traditional path into engineering. We value people who learned by building.

Location 

Remote. United States preferred; Also available to Canada, the United Kingdom, and Germany. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship or relocation for this role.

Explore Our Work 

Dive into the practical side of what we do at Chainguard. These resources provide a hands-on look at our processes and offer an opportunity for in-depth understanding of our product offerings and the technology behind them.

Chainguard Academy 

Base Salary Range

$205,000—$231,000 USD

About Us

We live and breathe our company values:

- We are customer obsessed — We focus on delivering solutions to our customers that create value and make their lives better.

- We have a bias for intentional action — We prioritize, plan, try things, and fail fast.

- We don't take ourselves too seriously (but we do serious work) — We are solving an important problem which takes focus, but we also like to enjoy the journey.

- We trust each other and assume good intentions — We're transparent with decisions to empower team members to make well informed decisions.

A few of the benefits we offer:

- Flexible & Remote-First Culture: Work remotely with team meetup opportunities, bi-annual destination summits, and a monthly stipend for coworking spaces, phone and internet costs.

- Our Approach to Equity: Receive stock options upon hire and promotion. Plus, you can participate in secondary offerings and have 10 years to exercise your options (yes, you read that correctly: 10 years!).

- 100% Covered Health Insurance: We cover 100% of your health, vision and dental insurance premiums for you and your dependents. Nothing comes out of your paycheck.

- ∞ Flexible Time Off: Take the time you need – to do our best work, we need to recharge and reset.

- 18 Weeks Paid Parental Leave: We offer 18 weeks for birthing parents and 12 weeks for non-birthing parents, with the option to use it all at once or throughout your child's first year.

If your experience is close but doesn't fulfill all requirements, please apply. We're building the best team in technology and are focused on hiring "Chainguardians" with unique backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences.

title: Senior Data Architect
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

- 
Datavail is hiring a Senior Data Architect to lead the design and delivery of modern data platforms for our clients

- You will own the architecture of client engagements from discovery through production, with a primary focus on Microsoft Fabric and the Azure data ecosystem

- You will define target-state architectures, build the data models that underpin them, and establish the SDLC and DevOps practices that let client teams operate and extend what we deliver

- This is a client-facing role

- You will work directly with business stakeholders, client IT and security teams, and Datavail delivery teams of data engineers, analytics engineers and BI developers, often across several engagements at once

RESPONSIBILITIES

- Architecture and solution design

- Lead discovery and current-state assessments of client data estates, including sources, integrations, platforms, data quality, security posture and operating model

- Define target-state and transition architectures for analytics, data warehousing, Lakehouse, real-time and operational data workloads

- Produce architecture deliverables: solution architecture documents, logical and physical architecture diagrams, architecture decision records (ADRs), non-functional requirements and capacity plans

- Evaluate platform and build-versus-buy trade-offs across Fabric, Databricks, Azure Synapse Analytics and Azure SQL, and present recommendations with cost, risk and effort clearly stated

- Apply the Azure Well-Architected Framework (reliability, security, cost optimization, operational excellence, performance efficiency) and the Cloud Adoption Framework's cloud-scale analytics guidance to every design

- Design for scale and multi-domain ownership, including data mesh and hub-and-spoke patterns where they fit the client's organization

- Plan and lead migrations from on-premises SQL Server, SSIS, SSAS and legacy data warehouses, and from Azure Synapse dedicated SQL pools, to Fabric and Azure

- Lead architecture and design reviews, maintain reference architectures and standards, manage exceptions, and track technical debt
Microsoft Fabric and Azure platform

- Architect end-to-end Fabric solutions across OneLake, Lakehouse, Warehouse, Data Factory pipelines, Dataflows Gen2, Spark notebooks, Real-Time Intelligence (Eventstream, Eventhouse, KQL) and Power BI

- Design OneLake strategy: workspace and domain structure, shortcuts to ADLS Gen2 and external storage, database mirroring, and medallion (bronze/silver/gold) layering on Delta Lake

- Size and govern Fabric capacities (F SKUs), including workload isolation, capacity monitoring, throttling behavior and cost management

- Forecast consumption, set budgets and tagging/showback standards, monitor unit economics, and optimize cloud/Fabric spend

- Design Power BI semantic models for performance and scale, including Direct Lake, Import and DirectQuery storage modes, composite models, incremental refresh, and row-level and object-level security

- Integrate Fabric with the wider Azure estate: ADLS Gen2, Azure Data Factory, Databricks and Unity Catalog, Azure SQL Database and Managed Instance, Cosmos DB, Event Hubs, Azure Functions and Azure Machine Learning

- Design network and identity controls: Microsoft Entra ID, managed identities and service principals, Azure Key Vault, private endpoints and Private Link, managed virtual networks and workspace-level access

- Data modeling

- Own conceptual, logical and physical data models for client solutions, from business glossary through to deployed schemas

- Apply the right modeling approach for each layer: Kimball dimensional modeling (star schemas, conformed dimensions, bus matrix, slowly changing dimensions Types 1, 2 and 6), Data Vault 2.0 (hubs, links, satellites) for integration layers, and normalized 3NF models for operational and master data

- Design canonical and enterprise data models, master and reference data structures, and entity resolution approaches

- Define naming standards, data type conventions, key strategies (surrogate, natural, hash), and partitioning and file layout for Delta tables

- Maintain models in a modeling tool (erwin Data Modeler, ER/Studio, SqlDBM or equivalent) and keep them in version control alongside code

- SDLC and DevOps

- Establish the delivery lifecycle for data workloads: environment strategy (dev, test, prod), branching and pull request standards, code review, release management and rollback

- Implement Fabric Git integration with Azure DevOps or GitHub, Fabric deployment pipelines, and automated deployment using the Fabric REST APIs and the fabric-cicd library

- Build CI/CD pipelines in Azure DevOps Pipelines and GitHub Actions for Fabric items, Azure Data Factory, Databricks (Asset Bundles), SQL database projects (DACPAC/sqlpackage) and Power BI (PBIP/TMDL)

- Define infrastructure as code with Bicep and Terraform for Azure resources, identities and networking

- Embed automated testing: unit tests for transformations, data quality and contract tests, schema-drift detection, and regression testing of semantic models

- Define DataOps practices for observability, alerting, lineage, pipeline SLAs and incident response, and hand them over with runbooks

- Define support models, SLAs/SLOs, escalation paths, training, documentation, and handoff criteria

- Work within Agile delivery (Scrum or Kanban) using Azure Boards or Jira, including backlog refinement, estimation and sprint planning

- Set standards for AI-assisted development with GitHub Copilot and AI coding agents across design, code, testing and documentation, including review and quality guardrails

- Data governance and security

- Design governance frameworks aligned to DAMA-DMBOK, covering data ownership and stewardship, metadata, data quality, lifecycle and retention

- Implement Microsoft Purview for data catalog, lineage, classification and sensitivity labels across Fabric and Azure sources

- Design least-privilege security models using Fabric workspace roles, item permissions, OneLake security, and row-, column- and object-level security

- Ensure solutions meet client regulatory obligations such as HIPAA, SOC 2, PCI DSS, GDPR and CCPA, working with client compliance and security teams

- Establish responsible AI and AI governance aligned to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the EU AI Act and Microsoft's Responsible AI Standard, including approved model use, data access policies for AI, and human oversight

- Design security controls for AI workloads, covering prompt injection, data exfiltration through agents, content filtering with Azure AI Content Safety, and Microsoft Purview data security for AI

- AI and machine learning enablement

- Design data foundations that support AI and machine learning: curated feature data, data quality controls and governed access for model training and inference

- Architect solutions that use Azure Machine Learning, Fabric Data Science and Azure OpenAI, including retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) over enterprise data with Azure AI Search

- Prepare client data estates and semantic models for Copilot in Fabric and Power BI

- Design Fabric IQ solutions, including ontologies that define business entities, relationships, rules and data bindings to lakehouses, eventhouses and Power BI semantic models, and Fabric data agents for conversational Q&A over ontology-grounded data
Model knowledge graphs for multi-hop reasoning over connected enterprise data, using Graph in Fabric and other graph technologies where appropriate

- Architect agentic solutions with Microsoft Foundry and Foundry IQ, using knowledge sources and knowledge bases that ground agents in both unstructured content and structured Fabric data

- Define where AI agents and models sit in the overall platform, including when to use Fabric, Foundry or Databricks, and how agents access governed data through APIs, tools and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers

- Design GenAIOps practices: evaluation of response quality and groundedness, tracing and observability, prompt and model versioning, and monitoring of token usage and cost

- Plan AI cost and capacity, including model selection, provisioned versus pay-as-you-go deployments, and the impact of AI workloads on Fabric and Databricks compute

- Consulting, pre-sales and delivery

- Support pre-sales: lead technical discovery calls, shape solution approaches, build effort estimates and contribute to proposals and statements of work (SOWs), including scope, assumptions, deliverables and acceptance criteria

- Fulfill the technical lead role on client engagements: own the technical approach and architecture standards, keep delivery aligned to scope and budget, serve as the primary technical contact for client teams, and raise risks and change requests early

- Review implementation against approved designs, conduct readiness reviews, and provide production sign-off

- Present architecture and recommendations to audiences from engineers to C-level executives, in writing and in person

- Identify follow-on opportunities and contribute to account growth based on client needs

- Develop solution accelerators and Datavail intellectual property (IP), such as reference architectures, reusable frameworks, deployment templates and packaged offerings, that speed up delivery and differentiate the practice

- Stay ahead of innovation across Microsoft Fabric, Azure and the wider data and AI market: evaluate preview and newly released capabilities, build proofs of concept, and turn what works into practice guidance and client recommendations

- Convert recurring patterns, decisions, and lessons learned into reusable Datavail intellectual property—including architecture blueprints, decision frameworks, assessment tools, checklists, templates, and accelerators—while protecting client confidentiality

- Leadership and mentoring

- Lead technical delivery teams of data engineers, analytics engineers and BI developers on client engagements

- Mentor team members through design reviews, code reviews, pairing and certification guidance
Contribute to hiring, interviewing and onboarding for the Data & Analytics practice

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems, engineering or a related field, or equivalent professional experience

- 10+ years of experience in data engineering, data warehousing or analytics, including 5+ years in a data or solution architect role

- 3+ years designing and delivering data solutions on Azure, and hands-on delivery experience with Microsoft Fabric in production

- End-to-end architecture ownership of at least two enterprise-scale data platform implementations

- Expert-level dimensional modeling skills and working knowledge of Data Vault 2.0 and normalized modeling

- Advanced SQL (T-SQL and Spark SQL) and working proficiency in Python/PySpark. Working knowledge of DAX and KQL

- Practical experience implementing CI/CD, Git-based workflows and infrastructure as code for data platforms

- Experience in a professional services, consulting or client-facing delivery environment, including pre-sales and estimation

- Experience leading and mentoring technical teams

- Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to produce clear architecture documentation and lead client workshops

- Ability to travel up to 25% to client sites

- Authorization to work in the United States 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

- Microsoft Certified: Fabric Data Engineer Associate (DP-700)

- Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert (AZ-305)

- Microsoft Certified: DevOps Engineer Expert (AZ-400)

- Databricks Certified Data Engineer Professional

- Delivered AI or machine learning solutions in production, including RAG or generative AI workloads on Azure

- Experience designing ontologies or knowledge graphs, and hands-on work with Fabric IQ or Foundry IQ

- Experience implementing AI governance or responsibl

Business Development Manager

Heb jij affiniteit met innovatieve optische- en meettechnologie en weet jij technische oplossingen te vertalen naar commerciële kansen? Krijg je daarnaast energie van het aanboren van nieuwe markten en het realiseren van groei? Dan zijn wij op zoek naar jou!

Als Business Development Manager ben je verantwoordelijk voor het stimuleren van de commerciële groei van onze Sensing Business in Europa. Je bent dé commerciële en interne gesprekspartner voor onze oplossingen op het gebied van licht-, display- en kleurmetingen. Je signaleert nieuwe marktkansen, ontwikkelt klantrelaties en helpt onze organisatie om onze positie binnen verschillende industrieën verder te versterken.

Je werkt nauw samen met onze salesteams, Marketing en de Europese Sensing-organisatie. Samen vertaal je ontwikkelingen in de markt en behoeften van klanten naar concrete commerciële mogelijkheden. Je opereert op Europees niveau, waarbij je regelmatig contact hebt met klanten en collega's in verschillende landen.

Wat ga je doen?

- Ontwikkelen en realiseren van commerciële groeiplannen en omzetdoelstellingen voor de toegewezen markt en productportfolio's;

- Actief identificeren van nieuwe marktkansen, potentiële klanten en strategische samenwerkingspartners.

- Opbouwen, onderhouden en uitbreiden van relaties met bestaande klanten en partners binnen Europa.

- Ontwikkelen van commerciële strategieën en proposities voor verschillende sectoren, waaronder automotive, manufacturing, food & agriculture, verlichting en displays, recycling, verf en kunststoffen.

- Ondersteunen van de lokale salesteams bij het identificeren, kwalificeren en ontwikkelen van commerciële kansen.

- Verzorgen en leiden van klantpresentaties, workshops, demonstraties en proof-of-concept trajecten.

- Optreden als inhoudelijk en commercieel adviseur voor klanten gedurende het volledige verkooptraject.

- Volgen van marktontwikkelingen, technologische innovaties en relevante wet- en regelgeving en deze vertalen naar commerciële kansen.

- Opstellen en bewaken van commerciële plannen, forecasts en pipeline-ontwikkelingen en hierover rapporteren aan het management.

- Nauw afstemmen met Europese collega's over nieuwe leads en commerciële trajecten, zodat kansen gezamenlijk en op de juiste manier worden opgepakt.

Wie ben jij?

- Je hebt minimaal een afgeronde HBO-opleiding, bij voorkeur in een technische richting zoals Engineering, Natuurkunde of Scheikunde. Een bedrijfskundige opleiding in combinatie met sterke technische affiniteit is ook passend.

- Je hebt minimaal 5 jaar ervaring in een commerciële functie binnen een technische B2B-omgeving, bijvoorbeeld in business development of technische sales.

- Je hebt ervaring met industriële meettechnologie en bij voorkeur kennis van kleurmeting, spectrofotometrie, colorimetrie en licht- en displaymetingen.

- Je hebt ervaring met het ontwikkelen van nieuwe markten en het uitbouwen van strategische klantrelaties.

- Je bent in staat om technische producteigenschappen te vertalen naar concrete klantbehoeften en commerciële oplossingen.

- Je hebt een ondernemende instelling, ziet kansen en neemt initiatief om deze te benutten.

- Je bent analytisch sterk en hebt ervaring met het opstellen van commerciële plannen, forecast en businesscases.

- Je bent communicatief vaardig en weet zowel technische specialisten als commerciële en managementstakeholders te overtuigen.

- Je beheerst de Engelse taal, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk. Beheersing van een andere Europese taal is een pré.

- Je bent gewend om internationaal en met verschillende afdelingen en culturen samen te werken.

- Je vindt het geen probleem om regelmatig te reizen binnen Europa.

Wat bieden we?

Een uitdagende, internationale functie binnen een innovatieve en groeiende business unit van een beursgenoteerde organisatie, waarin je volop ruimte krijgt om commerciële kansen te ontwikkelen en daadwerkelijk impact te maken.

Daarnaast bieden wij:

- Een aantrekkelijk salaris en een compleet pakket aan (secundaire) arbeidsvoorwaarden, waaronder een prestatiegerichte bonusregeling.

- Een zelfstandige en strategische rol met veel internationale contacten en verantwoordelijkheid.

- De mogelijkheid om mee te bouwen aan de verdere Europese groei van onze Sensing Business Unit.

- Een innovatieve werkomgeving met toegang tot hoogwaardige meettechnologie en een breed portfolio aan oplossingen.

- Ruimte voor persoonlijke ontwikkeling, trainingen en opleidingen.

- Een collegiale werkomgeving waarin samenwerking, kennisdeling en ondernemerschap centraal staan.

Wie zijn wij?

Konica Minolta is een internationaal bedrijf dat innovatieve oplossingen aan organisaties en de samenleving biedt. Het hoofdkantoor is gevestigd in Tokyo. Konica Minolta heeft haar groepsmaatschappijen in 50 landen met meer dan 35.000 werknemers. De organisatie biedt producten en diensten in 150 landen over de hele wereld.

Onze Mensen en Innovaties houden ons in beweging om onze business te versterken, continu ons motto 'Rethink and shape the future' toe te passen en de manier waarop mensen zakendoen en technologie inzetten te veranderen.

Iedere dag bij Konica Minolta is een kans om jouw Ideeën te delen, Verandering te stimuleren en samen te werken met collega's met verschillende achtergronden en ervaringen.

Together, we rethink today in order to shape the Future!

title: Vice President of Technology (US, Remote)
description:
Reports to: CTO

Department: Technology

Location: This is a fully remote U.S.-based position. Candidates must reside and work in one of the following states due to tax and compliance requirements: AR, AZ, CA, CO, FL, GA, ID, IL, LA, MD, MO, NC, NJ, NV, NY, OH, TX, VA, WA, WI, or WY.

Compensation: This position has geographic-based pay ranges. Final compensation and geographic tier placement are determined based on the candidate's primary work location, skills, experience, and qualifications.

Tier 1 (Higher Cost Markets): $190,000 - $220,000

Tier 2 (National Markets): $180,000 - $210,000

Tier 3 (Lower Cost Markets): $170,000 - $200,000

About the Company

Paleovalley and Wild Pastures were born from a simple but radical idea: real food can heal — people, animals, and the planet. When Paleovalley co-founders Autumn and Chas Smith saw how industrialized food was affecting human health and the health of the land, they refused to play along. Autumn’s own journey of healing through nutrient-dense foods lit a fire that became Paleovalley . From there, the mission grew roots, sprouted wings, and eventually expanded into Wild Pastures to bring regeneratively raised meats directly to families nationwide.

Today, Paleovalley crafts deeply nourishing snacks and supplements made with organic ingredients and honorable sourcing. Wild Pastures connects small American farmers practicing regenerative agriculture with customers who believe better food is worth fighting for. Every product, every partnership, and every decision is guided by a commitment to real ingredients, regenerative practices, and the belief that health is built from the soil up.

We’re a team of grounded doers, curious thinkers, bold builders, and warm humans who like to laugh while doing meaningful work. We're growing quickly, fueled by purpose and a shared desire to repair the food system one thoughtful choice at a time. If you feel energized by impact, drawn to mission, and ready to join a company rewriting the future of food, we’d love to meet you!

About the Opportunity

The technology behind Paleovalley and Wild Pastures is central to how customers shop, subscribe, and get help - and how our teams fulfill orders and run the business. Much of it was built in-house by our co-founder and CTO. As both brands grow, we need a technology organization that can keep these platforms strong, connect them with our business systems, and support the next stage of growth. 

The Vice President of Technology will be the CTO’s trusted right hand and lead the full technology function across software engineering, business systems, and IT. This leader will set priorities and investment plans with the CTO, make consequential day-to-day decisions with substantial autonomy, and own the team, budget, delivery, and health of our technology. The role gives the CTO room to focus on company-wide direction and the technical work where he can add the most value.

Success here requires executive judgment, real technical depth, and a practical approach to AI and automation. You’ll work through architecture, code, and difficult incidents while building shared knowledge and ownership across the team. You’ll also guide AI adoption that improves how we build software and run the business, partnering with E-Commerce on reliable solutions for the shopping experience and commercial priorities.

What You’ll Do

Technology Strategy and Leadership

- Set the technology strategy and multi-year roadmap with the CTO, turning business priorities into clear investments, sequencing, and delivery across both brands.

- Lead engineering, business systems, and IT as one function, developing leaders, clarifying decision rights, and building the capacity needed for growth.

- Own the technology budget, staffing, and vendor strategy; make sound build-versus-buy decisions and raise enterprise-level risks and architectural choices with the CTO.

- Establish and oversee a centralized technology request intake and prioritization process, evaluating incoming requests, defining project scope, assessing business impact, allocating resources, and communicating realistic timelines to stakeholders across departments.

- Develop scalable engineering workflows and project management practices that improve accountability, delivery predictability, and cross-functional communication without introducing unnecessary administrative complexity.

Custom Platforms and Engineering

- Own the architecture and engineering delivery of our custom commerce, subscription, customer service, and internal platforms, balancing new capabilities with reliability and maintainability.

- Stay close to the technical work through design and code reviews, hands-on troubleshooting, and selective coding when a critical problem calls for it.

- Set practical standards for testing, releases, monitoring, and incident response so teams can move quickly while protecting the customer and employee experience.

- Reduce dependence on any one person by documenting critical systems, sharing ownership, cross-training the team, and testing recovery procedures.

AI and Automation

- Lead AI and automation strategy with the CTO, turning emerging capabilities into practical agents, workflows, and tools that improve efficiency, decision-making, and organizational capacity.

- Evaluate where AI, conventional automation, and human expertise are best applied, measuring business value before scaling adoption across engineering and business functions.

Business Systems, IT and Security

- Lead the strategy for business applications, integrations, and data flows that connect commerce with customer service, fulfillment, manufacturing, supply chain, and finance.

- Oversee IT services, infrastructure, access, cybersecurity, privacy, and vendor risk, including practical standards for AI reliability, data protection, and appropriate human oversight.

- Evaluate clinical EHR vignettes paired with a question, a proposed answer, and a distractor “trap” answer across diagnosis and treatment tasks, spanning cardiovascular, nervous, hematologic, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, musculoskeletal, and integumentary systems;

Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid ​

You decide when and how much to contribute. For this project, tasks are estimated at around 10–20 hours per week during active phases. title: Director of Clinical Case Management
description:
Applicants must reside in California 

LEAP is seeking a Director of Clinical Case Management to provide agency-wide leadership and oversight of its case management, social work, and clinical services. This leader will be responsible for case management quality, staff leadership and clinical supervision, service delivery, regulatory compliance, and the continued development of a coordinated, person-centered clinical model for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

The Director will lead and develop LEAP’s social work team, supervise an Associate Director of Clinical Case Management if the position is established, establish clinical standards and practices, and ensure high-quality, consistent services across regions. Working closely with the CEO and other department leaders, the Director will use clinical expertise, data, and quality measures to strengthen services, address complex needs, and support LEAP’s continued growth.

What You'll Do

1. Case Management Leadership, Clinical Supervision & Team Development

- Lead, supervise, coach, and develop LEAP's social work/clinical team, including supervision of an Associate Director of Clinical Case Management, if established, to support agency-wide clinical operations and day-to-day implementation.

- Provide clinical supervision to assigned staff and partner with an external clinical consultant to ensure appropriate clinical supervision across the team, consistent with Board of Behavioral Sciences (BBS) requirements and professional standards.

- Maintain an active presence in the field, observing staff practice, reviewing cases and plans, and coaching staff to strengthen clinical judgment and service quality.

- Monitor caseloads, workload, staff capacity, and clinical practice across regions.

- Lead case consultation and support social workers in complex cases, crises, and situations requiring higher-level clinical judgment.

- Identify training and professional-development needs for staff and providers and build team capacity to deliver LEAP's clinical model consistently.

2. Case Management Implementation & Service Oversight

- Oversee implementation of clinical programs, protocols, and service standards across regions.

- Ensure clinical assessments, intake, care planning, case management, home visits, crisis planning, and service coordination are delivered consistently and appropriately in collaboration with the Residential Services department.

- Ensure clinical services match each client’s assessed needs and are effectively integrated into their care plan.

- Oversee clinical and therapeutic consultant services, ensuring appropriate referral, utilization, coordination, and quality.

- Provide oversight of crisis response and agency-wide on-call program, ensuring that appropriate protocols, escalation channels, staff readiness, and follow-through processes are in place and effective.

- Supervise and guide the Associate Director in coordinating agency-wide clinical operations and initiatives, specialist services, workflow, and day-to-day implementation of clinical standards and practices.

- Collaborate with Residential Services, Operations, Quality & Compliance, home providers, and other partners to support coordinated service delivery.

3. Case Management Strategy & Program Development

- Partner with the CEO to establish LEAP's case management strategy and clinical priorities aligned with client and provider needs, organizational goals, and growth.

- Lead the ongoing development and refinement of LEAP's case management service model and related clinical supports, including clear program goals, KPIs, and quality and impact measures.

- Develop and maintain case management and clinical program guides, protocols, standards, and practice expectations that translate the model into consistent service delivery.

- Use evidence-based practices, regulatory requirements, organizational data, and client, provider, and staff experiences to strengthen case management and clinical practices.

- Identify emerging clinical needs and opportunities for new or enhanced services, interventions, and partnerships.

4. Quality, Outcomes & Continuous Improvement

- Establish meaningful clinical quality, service, and outcome measures aligned with LEAP's clinical model and organizational KPIs.

- Oversee and monitor clinical documentation, service delivery, caseload trends, utilization, outcomes, incidents, and other quality and effectiveness indicators.

- Use data, case reviews, compliance findings, client, provider, and staff experience and feedback to identify trends, risks, gaps, and opportunities for improvement.

- Ensure clinical practices meet applicable regulatory, licensing, Regional Center, ethical, and organizational requirements.

- Translate findings into improvements for clinical protocols, training, staffing, services, and program design.

5. Partnerships, Cross-Functional Leadership & Board Support

- Partner with department leaders to address cross-functional needs affecting clinical services, clients, home providers, and staff.

- Build and maintain relationships with Regional Centers, clinical providers, community organizations, and other strategic partners.

- Represent LEAP's clinical model, priorities, and needs in appropriate external meetings and partnerships.

- Provide the CEO and Board with clinical trends, outcomes, risks, and program updates as requested.

- Contribute clinical expertise to organizational planning, growth, and agencywide policy development.

Education:

- Master's degree in Social Work (MSW) from an accredited institution.

- Current California LCSW license in good standing.

- Meets applicable California BBS requirements to provide clinical supervision to associate clinicians.

Experience:

- 10-15 years of significant progressive experience in social work, behavioral health, clinical services, or related human-services settings, including experience supervising and developing professional staff.

- Demonstrated experience overseeing clinical programs, case management/service coordination, quality, and complex cases.

- Experience serving individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities and/or individuals with complex behavioral health needs strongly preferred.

- Knowledge of California's developmental disabilities service system, Regional Centers, the Lanterman Act, applicable Title 17/Title 22 requirements, and related regulatory requirements strongly preferred.

- Strong analytical skills and demonstrated ability to use clinical and operational data to assess quality, identify trends, and improve services.

- Strong leadership, communication, judgment, collaboration, and change-management skills.

title: Director of AI and Enterprise Architecture
description:
Director of AI and Enterprise Architecture

Remote – Western US (Pacific or Mountain time zone preferred)

Why Us

NewRocket is a ServiceNow Elite Partner and a Claude Select partner, helping enterprises reimagine how work gets done with ServiceNow and AI. We work with public and private sector organizations, including some of the world’s biggest brands, to simplify processes, remove complexity, and turn the promise of AI into measurable business outcomes. We are “Raising the Bar” in delivering technology’s promise to create new kinds of experiences for our customers.

Our Core Values: Excellence, Creativity, Integrity, Teamwork and Empathy #ExCITE . At NewRocket , these values guide everything we do: they are the foundation of our culture and define how we Go Beyond for our clients.

The Role

About the role

We're hiring a Director of AI and Enterprise Architecture to be the technical leader on our client engagements, working alongside our forward deployed engineers as they build and deploy agentic AI inside complex enterprise environments. This is a billable, client-facing consulting role.

Large enterprises don't run on one system. They run on decades of layered platforms: ERP backbones like SAP and Oracle, service and workflow platforms like ServiceNow, CRM, HR and finance suites, custom integrations, data warehouses, and the identity and security controls that hold it all together. Agentic AI only creates value when it can work safely inside that landscape: reading the right data, taking the right actions, respecting approvals and access controls, and leaving an audit trail that satisfies IT, security and compliance.

On each engagement, you're the person who understands that landscape. You map the client's systems, translate their business goals into the architecture and requirements agents need, and lead the forward deployed engineers through it as they build, so workflows make it out of pilot and into the client's production environment.

What you'll do

- 
Lead engagements technically. Serve as the senior technical leader on client engagements, setting architecture direction and guiding the forward deployed engineers who are building alongside you.

- 
Map the client's system landscape. Quickly get to grips with each client's environment, including ServiceNow, SAP, Oracle, Salesforce, Workday, custom systems and the integrations between them, and turn it into a clear picture the engineering team can build against.

- 
Translate business processes into agent-ready requirements. Work with client process owners to break down workflows like incident resolution, procure-to-pay, order-to-cash and employee onboarding into the tasks, data, decisions, permissions and human approval points an agent must handle.

- 
Design how agents connect to systems of record. Define the integration approach for each engagement: APIs, integration platforms, event streams, MCP and tool-calling layers, and data access patterns.

- 
Get workflows into production. Navigate the client's environments, change management, release processes, testing, monitoring and support handoff so agentic workflows move from pilot to production.

- 
Clear the path with security and governance. Design identity and access models for agents (service accounts, least privilege, delegated authority), audit logging and controls, and win sign-off from client CISOs, risk teams and auditors.

- 
Advise senior client stakeholders. Act as a trusted architecture advisor to client CIOs, CTOs, enterprise architects and platform owners, and identify where agentic workflows can expand into new use cases.

- 
Strengthen the practice. Turn what you learn on engagements into reusable blueprints, integration playbooks and readiness assessments, and share field insight with our product and engineering teams.

What you bring

- 7 to 10 years of experience in enterprise architecture, solution architecture or technical leadership roles within large, complex enterprise software environments.

- Deep hands-on knowledge of at least two major enterprise platforms, such as ServiceNow, SAP (S/4HANA, BTP), Oracle (Fusion, E-Business Suite, OCI), Salesforce or Workday, including their data models, APIs, extension frameworks and upgrade constraints.

- Strong grounding in enterprise integration: REST and SOAP APIs, middleware and iPaaS (MuleSoft, Boomi, SAP Integration Suite or similar), event-driven architecture, and master data management.

- Practical experience with AI or automation in production, such as LLM-based applications, agentic workflows, RPA or intelligent automation, and a clear point of view on where agents fit and where they don't.

- Proven track record moving enterprise systems from design to production, including environment management, SDLC and change control, testing, monitoring and operational support.

You will build C-suite trust, perform deep discovery to map the customer's political and technical landscape, and scope the value. title: Machine Learning Engineer - IV (Biometrics)
description:
Headquarters: India (remote)

Role Purpose 

We’re looking for a Staff/Senior Machine Learning Engineer with deep expertise in computer vision and biometrics to lead the design and scaling of face recognition systems in production. You’ll build and train models, and own ML systems end-to-end on AWS. The final job level for this role will be determined following the interview process.

What You’ll Do 

Lead the design and development of computer vision systems for biometrics (face attributes, detection, quality, and recognition)
Rigorous fairness analysis and benchmarking of biometric models across various datasets and operating conditions.
Architect, train, and optimize models using PyTorch, Tensorflow, and/or JAX
Own and evolve end-to-end ML pipelines, from data ingestion to deployment. Design automated pipelines (Airflow) for data ingestion and cleaning. You will be responsible for curating balanced training sets and generating synthetic data to address both quality and diversity gaps.
Production Engineering: Own the path to production. Optimize models for low-latency inference (quantization, distillation, TensorRT/ONNX) and manage deployment on AWS.
Mentor ML engineers, conduct code/design reviews, and drive technical best practices across the Computer Vision team.

What We’re Looking For 

Experience: 5+ years of industry experience in Machine Learning, with at least 3 years dedicated to Biometrics or Face Analysis.
Deep expertise in computer vision and biometrics, especially face recognition.
Fairness & Ethics: You understand the sources of algorithmic bias in Computer Vision and have practical experience measuring and mitigating disparate impact.
Strong Engineering: Expert proficiency in Python (both machine learning and vision libraries such as Pillow, OpenCV, PyTorch, etc). You write clean, modular, production-ready code.
Systems Architecture: Experience designing end-to-end ML pipelines (Data to Train to Deploy) and working with workflow orchestrators like Airflow.
Cloud Native: Hands-on experience scaling training jobs on multi-GPU clusters and deploying services on AWS (SageMaker, EC2, EKS).

Nice to Have 

Research Publications: Papers in CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, or FG related to face recognition, image quality assessment, or fairness.
Large Scale Search: Experience with vector databases (e.g., Milvus, Faiss) and approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search algorithms.
Familiarity with privacy, security, and compliance in biometric systems.
Mobile/Edge Experience: Experience porting models to edge or mobile devices utilizing frameworks such as CoreML, LiteRT, and/or TFLite.
Synthetic Data: Experience using GANs or diffusion models to generate synthetic faces for training.
Strong communication skills.

Jumio Values: 

IDEAL: Integrity, Diversity, Empowerment, Accountability, Leading Innovation 

Equal Opportunities : 

Jumio is a collaboration of people with different ideas, strengths, interests and cultures. We welcome applications and colleagues from all backgrounds and of all statuses.

Jumio is a B2B technology company dedicated to eradicating online identity fraud, money laundering and other financial crimes to help make the internet safer. title: Director of Security Engineering
description:
Headquarters: Remote - USA

About the Role

Abnormal AI protects organizations from the most sophisticated email and collaboration attacks using behavioral AI. Security is not a bolt-on at Abnormal; it is core to the product we sell and the trust our customers place in us. Our security organization operates a commercial cloud environment and a separate FedRAMP-authorized environment, and we are pursuing increasingly rigorous federal authorizations as we grow.

We are hiring a Director of Security reporting to the CISO and leading the Security Engineering organization. You will build and scale high-performing security teams, own major security programs end to end, and operate autonomously in the CISO's absence, including representing security to executive leadership, customers, and auditors.

This is a role for a deeply technical leader with a software engineering background who has grown into people leadership. You have built security teams from the ground up, you write and review code and architecture when it matters, and you believe the best security organizations earn their influence through partnership rather than policy enforcement.

Our Security Philosophy

We run security the way the best engineering-led companies do:

- Security reduces toil. Our job is to make the rest of the company faster and safer at the same time. If a control adds friction without reducing risk, it is a defect.

- Paved paths, safe by default. We invest in guardrails, golden paths, and secure-by-default infrastructure so the easy choice is the secure choice. We prefer preventing classes of problems over chasing individual findings.

- Partnership over gatekeeping. Security succeeds only through deep collaboration with engineering, IT, and business teams. We embed with builders, we ship alongside them, and we take on their constraints as our own.

- Engineering-grade rigor. We treat security problems as engineering problems: automated, measurable, code-reviewed, and continuously improved.

If the security cultures that value freedom and responsibility, context over control, and guardrails over gates resonate with you, you will feel at home here.

What You Will Do

- Serve as deputy to the CISO: act with full authority in the CISO's absence and represent the security organization to executives, customers, and regulators.

- Lead, coach, and grow managers and senior engineers across Security Engineering and Security Operations.

- Own the security engineering roadmap: cloud security architecture (AWS-first), detection and response, identity, vulnerability management, and secure-by-default platform investments.

- Drive cross-functional programs with Engineering, IT, and Product, from AI security governance to data perimeter controls to federal compliance initiatives.

- Set and defend engineering standards for the security organization: everything as code, automated where possible, measured against outcomes rather than activity.

- Build hiring pipelines and raise the bar on every hire; own performance management, promotion cases, and succession planning within your teams.

- Translate technical risk into business terms for the executive team and board, and translate business priorities into a coherent security strategy.

Must Haves

- 10+ years in security or software engineering, including 4+ years managing security teams, ideally including managers of managers or equivalent scope.

- A genuine software engineering background: you have shipped production software, and you evaluate security solutions the way an engineer would.

- A proven record of building and scaling high-performing security teams, with alumni who would work for you again.

- Deep technical fluency in cloud-native environments: AWS organizations and multi-account governance, Kubernetes, identity and access, detection engineering, and modern SDLC security.

- Demonstrated cross-functional leadership: you have earned the trust of engineering leaders and shipped security outcomes through their teams, not around them.

- Strong written communication: you produce decision-ready documents and can drive alignment asynchronously.

- Executive presence: comfortable presenting to C-level leadership, customers, and auditors without preparation from the CISO.

Strong Signals

- You are currently a security engineering manager or senior manager at a fintech, high-growth startup, or forward-leaning enterprise, and you are ready for broader scope.

- You have built paved-path or secure-by-default platforms that measurably reduced both risk and developer friction.

- Experience with compliance-driven environments (FedRAMP, SOC 2, ISO 27001) without letting compliance define the security program.

- Experience securing AI/ML systems or governing AI adoption at scale.

- You have operated in environments where security headcount was scarce and automation was the only way to scale.

Why This Role

You will inherit strong teams, an executive staff that treats security as a first-class function, and a CISO who wants a true partner rather than a lieutenant. The scope is broad, the autonomy is real, and the ceiling on this role is defined by what you take on.

title: Software Engineer - Query Execution
description:
Headquarters: Portugal - Remote

Be Part of Building the Future 

Dremio is the unified lakehouse platform for self-service analytics and AI, serving hundreds of global enterprises, including Maersk, Amazon, Regeneron, NetApp, and S&P Global. Customers rely on Dremio for cloud, hybrid, and on-prem lakehouses to power their data mesh, data warehouse migration, data virtualization, and unified data access use cases. Based on open source technologies, including Apache Iceberg and Apache Arrow, Dremio provides an open lakehouse architecture enabling the fastest time to insight and platform flexibility at a fraction of the cost. Learn more at www.dremio.com. 

About the role 
Dremio’s Query Execution team builds the runtime responsible for executing analytical queries at scale. The team sits between query planning and table scans, building the systems that turn query plans into efficient, reliable execution.

As a Software Engineer, you’ll work with experienced engineers to build, test, and support well-scoped improvements to the execution engine. You’ll learn how Dremio’s query runtime works while contributing to areas such as query operators, expression evaluation, memory management, scheduling, and performance.

What you’ll be doing 

- Build and support execution-engine components: Implement, test, debug, and maintain well-defined changes to query operators, expression evaluation, execution scheduling, and resource management.

- Develop reliable software: Write clear, maintainable Java code; add unit and integration tests; and follow established engineering practices for code review, testing, and documentation.

- Investigate issues: Help diagnose query correctness, reliability, and performance issues using query profiles, logs, telemetry, benchmarks, and production data.

- Learn runtime and performance fundamentals: Build familiarity with vectorized processing, concurrency, memory usage, parallelism, data exchange, and disk spilling.

- Collaborate with the team: Work closely with senior engineers and partner teams to understand requirements, break work into manageable tasks, and deliver incremental improvements.

- Use AI-assisted development tools: Apply AI tools to code comprehension, debugging, test generation, and documentation, while validating results through testing, review, and sound engineering judgment.

- Grow your engineering skills: Participate actively in design discussions and code reviews, seek feedback, and steadily take on broader technical responsibility.

What we’re looking for 

- Software engineering foundation: Up to two years of professional software development experience, or equivalent experience through internships, coursework, or substantial personal projects.

- Programming skills: Proficiency in Java or another object-oriented programming language; willingness to learn and work in a large Java codebase.

- Computer science fundamentals: Understanding of data structures, algorithms, and basic concurrency concepts.

- Problem-solving ability: Able to work through well-defined technical problems, ask good questions, and apply feedback to reach a solution.

- Quality mindset: Commitment to writing tested, maintainable code and learning established development, testing, and review practices.

- Communication and collaboration: Able to communicate progress, surface blockers early, and work effectively with teammates.

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Bonus points if you have 

- 

- Exposure to database internals, query processing, distributed systems, or large-scale data processing.

- Familiarity with performance-oriented software concepts such as profiling, memory management, concurrency, or vectorized processing.

- Experience with C++, Apache Arrow, Parquet, Apache Iceberg, Spark, Hadoop, or cloud object stores.

- Contributions to open-source projects.

What we value 

At Dremio, we hold ourselves to high standards when it comes to People, Thinking, and Action. Our Gnarlies (that's what we call our employees) communicate with clarity, drive accountability, and are respectful towards each other. We confront brutal facts and focus on results while operating with a sense of urgency and building a "flywheel". People who like to jump in and drive momentum will thrive in our #GnarlyLife. 

Dremio is an equal opportunity employer supporting workforce diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, marital status, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other unlawful factor. 

Dremio is committed to providing any necessary accommodations for individuals with disabilities within our application and interview process. To request accommodation due to a disability, please inform your recruiter. 

Dremio has policies in place to protect the personal information that employees and applicants disclose to us. Please click here to review the privacy notice. 

Important Security Notice for Candidates 

At Dremio, we uphold trust and transparency as paramount values in all our interactions with customers, partners, employees, and the general public. We have been targeted by individuals creating fake domains similar to ours to scam prospects and candidates. Please note that all official communications from us will be from an @dremio.com domain. If you suspect you've been targeted by a scam, it's imperative to report the incident to your local law enforcement agencies. For more information about this type of scam, please refer to Dremio's official statement here . 

Dremio is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited resumes and will not pay fees to any third-party agency or company that does not have a signed agreement with the Company.

title: Abuse Research Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Remote from the US

Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career. 

About the team

Abuse Research Group (ARG) handles proactive threat hunting and adversary behavior analysis across Stripe products. Rather than reacting to alerts, the team maps end-to-end fraud and abuse paths, validates novel attack vectors, and identifies product conditions that enable fraud. Using agentic automated testing and simulation tools, ARG translates research into actionable threat advisories, strategic control recommendations, and regression scenarios to systematically eliminate vulnerabilities.

What you’ll do

As an Abuse Research Engineer in the Abuse Research Group, you will play a critical role in safeguarding Stripe’s financial ecosystem by proactively hunting for advanced threats, dissecting complex fraud vectors, and extracting actionable adversary intelligence. Rather than relying solely on reactive alerts, you will develop and execute hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations across internal telemetry and external sources to uncover fraudulent tools, tactics, and techniques (TTPs) before they impact Stripe’s platform. Central to this work is FT3 (Fraud Taxonomy 3.0), Stripe’s multi-layered taxonomy that decomposes monolithic fraud into structured kill chains. Collaborating cross-functionally with Fraud Ops, Strategy, Risk, Onboarding, and Security, you will integrate threat intelligence, build agentic simulation workflows, and systematically eliminate product vulnerabilities.

Responsibilities

- Proactive Threat Hunting & Kill Chain Analysis: Formulate hypotheses and conduct iterative threat hunting operations across Stripe systems and external data.

- FT3 Taxonomy: Apply and enrich the FT3 framework across empirical datasets and incidents, standardizing threat intelligence across kill chain phases and targeted API endpoints. 

- Threat Intelligence & Signal Expansion: Partner with teams like Fraud Intelligence to integrate, curate, and automate threat feeds into engineering workflows. 

- Cross-Functional Advisories & Strategic Controls: Translate raw research and retrospective findings into actionable threat advisories and control recommendations (policy, technical systems, support workflows, and detection mechanisms) for stakeholders across Fraud, Risk, Onboarding, and Security. 

- Agentic Testing & Adversary Simulation: Utilize agentic automated testing frameworks to simulate adversary TTPs, validate whether deployed controls interrupt empirical kill chains, and generate regression scenarios to exercise controls. 

Who you are 

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 

Minimum requirements

- 5+ years of experience conducting threat intelligence, threat hunting, or technical incident response within cyber security, product abuse, or trust domains. 

- 5+ years of experience analyzing large, complex datasets using data analytics tools to identify anomalies, map behavioral trends, and solve complex fraud problems. 

- B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. 

- Expert proficiency in Python and SQL, with demonstrated experience using code and scripting to automate workflows, build investigative tools, or query big data pipelines. 

- Hands-on experience in log analysis (e.g., application logs, API route telemetry, network security events), digital forensics, and cyber investigation methodologies. 

- Strong communication skills with a proven ability to translate complex technical research into clear, actionable recommendations and advisories for cross-functional partners.

Preferred qualifications 

- Deep technical understanding of threat actor motivations, infrastructure, and TTPs specific to financial fraud (e.g., ATO, Card Testing, Credential Stuffing).

title: Principal Product Management, Growth
description:
Headquarters: Remote

ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute. You’ll make things happen fast.

Principal Product Manager, Growth

About ZoomInfo

ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You'll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won't just contribute — you'll make things happen, fast.

The Opportunity

Own a Growth Portfolio and Set the Pattern the Rest of the Team Inherits

ZoomInfo built the industry's most sophisticated GTM data platform. The next frontier is turning every visitor into revenue without waiting on a human handoff — a coherent self-serve journey that activates a non-customer in minutes, converts consumption into upgrade, and routes high-intent signals back to sales when a human will close more than they distract.

You'll define the multi-quarter thesis on which channels compound, the operating rhythm the rest of the growth PM team inherits, and the ZoomInfo POV on how buyers discover us in an AI-first world.

The impact is immediate and compounding. Every signup you activate, every credit you cause to be consumed, every transaction, every PQL you route, every "buy more" event you trigger is revenue — and every operating pattern you set multiplies across the growth PM group. We've adopted a consumption-first monetization model and a unified entry-point thesis across the company, and we run weekly: if your hypothesis can't be falsified inside a sprint, it isn't a hypothesis. This is a rare opportunity to own a P&L-shaped surface with full air cover to ship fast, learn in public, re-pivot when the data turns — and to define the growth PM craft as ZoomInfo scales it.

What You'll Do

Own the Portfolio End-to-End

Take a portfolio-scope growth surface — and own it from first impression to revenue. Define the entry points, the activation milestones, the monetization moments, and the sales-assist signals across the channels that make up the portfolio. Drive the user experience across surfaces: landing, signup, in-product onboarding, empty states, upgrade modals, paywalls, lifecycle communication, and the agent-readable / LLM-discovery surfaces that are becoming primary. You own the funnel chart; you own the why behind every drop.

Set the Multi-Quarter Growth Thesis

Beyond weekly experiments, own 4-8 quarter bets on which channels compound and which retire. Publish a written POV on where PLG distribution is heading (LLM-first discovery, MCP-as-channel, agent-readable onboarding, partner-driven trials) and defend the sequencing to the exec team. Rebalance investment across the portfolio quarterly based on unit economics, not the loudest channel.

Run Experimentation as the Operating Rhythm — and Set the Rhythm for the Team

Ship 8-10 experiments per sprint. Pre-register the hypothesis, the metric, the success threshold, and — critically — the invalidation signal. Read results weekly, kill what doesn't work, double down on what does, and keep a written record so the team compounds learning instead of repeating it. Your rubric, your retro format, and your invalidation-signal standard become the template the rest of the Growth PM group inherits. Translate results into concrete changes: copy rewrites, schema tweaks, pricing changes, new flows, retired ones. Close the loop with engineering, design, and analytics inside the same week.

Design Self-Serve as a First-Class Path

Most users on your portfolio never speak to sales before they hit a "buy more" moment. Your in-product copy, paywall framing, empty states, activation paths, and upgrade triggers are the product. Apply growth-engineering rigor — credit economics, consumption pacing, signal routing, lifecycle messaging, intelligent gating — so the right offer lands in front of the right user at exactly the right moment. Hand high-intent users to sales with a clean signal; absorb low-intent users with a clean self-serve path.

Diagnose the Funnel With Data, Not Vibes

Data is your default tool, not a thing you ask analytics to do for you. You independently analyze the funnel, segment the cohort, find the leak, and propose the fix — then validate it with an experiment. You know when to trust a 5% lift and when to call it noise. Just as important: you know when to zoom out from a specific funnel drop to a portfolio-level rebalance, and can defend that call.

Shape the Monetization Mechanic

You'll design the credit economics of your portfolio: what's free, what's gated, what gets a "buy more" prompt, what triggers a PQL. You'll model the unit economics — credit cost, revenue per credit, upgrade rate, expansion rate — and you'll defend the pricing decisions in front of finance and sales leadership with the math.

Orchestrate Across Sales, Marketing, and CS

Self-serve doesn't mean alone. You'll route PQLs into the right hands (AE, SC, AM, or no one), partner with marketing on acquisition and lifecycle, and work with CS to understand why activated users churn before upgrade. You'll run the operating cadences that keep your portfolio aligned with the broader PLG portfolio without becoming a meeting machine.

Multiply the Team

Help hire and calibrate the Sr Growth PMs owning adjacent loops. Coach them into ownership. Your retro is their template; your experiment quality is their bar. Raise the craft of the whole Growth PM group as it scales.

Stay Honest About What's Working

Write retrospectives that name the wrong calls as cleanly as the right ones. Update your priors publicly when the data turns. Hold strong opinions weakly. The team that ships the most experiments isn't the team that's right the most — it's the team that updates the fastest.

What You'll Bring

- 8–12 years of product management experience, with 4+ years specifically in growth, PLG, or self-serve product roles

- Direct P&L ownership at portfolio scope — a loop or portfolio you've driven from $Y with your name on the number, not a feature inside someone else's loop

- Experience presenting to CEO / CRO / CFO / board on growth mechanics — the credit-economics deck, the funnel narrative, the "kill this bet" moment

- Track record of hiring, mentoring, or calibrating other growth PMs — comfortable being the bar

- You're a builder. You ship landing pages, signup flows, and in-product experiments — not specs that sit in Jira. You sit with designers and engineers, write copy, and prototype with code.

- AI-fluent with a public POV. You understand that LLMs are becoming a primary discovery surface. You have opinions — publishable ones — about agent-readable flows, MCP-as-distribution, GEO/AEO, and how an AI agent's recommendation impacts a funnel.

- Marketing-fluent. You hold your own with SEO, paid acquisition, content, and lifecycle marketing teams as a peer, not a consumer.

- Demonstrated track record of running structured experimentation (A/B tests, multivariate, holdouts, pre/post) at sprint cadence — including at cohort sizes where 50/50 doesn't have power

- Strong analytics fluency — comfortable in Snowflake without analyst hand-holding

- Working knowledge of consumption-based pricing, credit economics, freemium mechanics, and PQL frameworks

- B2B SaaS background; data, GTM, or sales-tech domain experience is a plus but not required

Who You Are

Core Competencies

Funnel Foundation. Expert-level understanding of full-funnel growth. You can reason about activation rates, time-to-value, retention curves, credit economics, upgrade triggers, and PQL signal quality with depth. You've owned a growth loop — or portfolio — in production. SQL and analytics fluency let you diagnose a funnel drop, prototype the fix, and validate it in the same week.

Portfolio Thinking. You reason about ToF (or an equivalent surface) as a portfolio of channels with different unit economics, decay curves, and compounding dynamics — not a single funnel. You rebalance investment quarterly based on where marginal dollars return the most, and you can defend the rebalance to leadership with the math.

Experimentation Discipline. You don't ship without a hypothesis. You pre-register the metric and the invalidation signal before the test runs. You read results honestly, kill losing variants without ego, and document learnings so the team compounds knowledge instead of relitigating settled questions. You know the difference between an experiment and a launch — and you can tell when each is the right move.

Category POV. You have a public, defensible point of view on where PLG distribution is heading — agent-readable surfaces, MCP-as-channel, GEO/AEO, LLM-first onboarding — grounded in benchmarks from peer companies (Clay, Linear, Vercel, Cursor, Notion), not just internal data. That POV shows up in the roadmap.

Distribution Mindset. Experience designing growth surfaces where sales teams, marketing teams, and self-serve users are simultaneously your customers. You measure success through revenue, consumption, and expansion velocity, not screens shipped. You understand growth economics: each additional entry point, freemium offer, or AI trial compounds in value through shared activation patterns, amortized acquisition costs, and recurring consumption network effects.

Operational Velocity. You read the funnel daily, not quarterly. You prototype emerging mechanics — paywalls, in-app prompts, lifecycle sequences — to understand their practical constraints before committing engineering time. You hold strong opinions weakly, updating your design assumptions as evidence accumulates, publicly, even when the prior thesis was your own.

Strategic Communication. You translate between funnel depth and business impact fluently. You can explain to the CEO why a credit pricing change is worth a quarter of work. You can communicate to engineers why a revenue constraint requires a "quiet release" in two weeks rather than a polished launch in three months. You influence without formal authority through forcing functions, falsifiable invalidation signals, and earned credibility.

Talent Leverage. You coach Sr PMs into full ownership of their loops. Your retro is their template. Your experiment quality is their bar. You help hire the next PMs on the team, and you calibrate — you know what "great" looks like at Sr level and you can articulate the gap to someone who isn't there yet.

Copy Instinct. Microcopy is part of your craft, not someone else's job. You can rewrite a paywall headline, an upgrade modal, an empty state, or an onboarding CTA on instinct — and defend the rewrite with PLG principles. You know when to ask content design for help and when to ship the rewrite yourself.

The Environment

Reporting, Pace & Impact

Reporting & Collaboration. Report to the VP Product, PLG. Peer to the Sr Directors of Marketing, Sales Operations, and Customer Success on the growth contracts (PQL routing, demand-gen alignment, credit economics). Work shoulder-to-shoulder with the engineering and design leaders building the underlying surfaces, the GTM leaders routing PQLs into sales, and a peer PM group covering monetization, lifecycle, viral, onboarding, and analytics. Regular exposure to the CEO, CRO, CMO, and CFO — you own those conversations at your level.

Pace & Problems. Fast-moving teams that understand the space. Weekly experimentation cadence layered under 4-quarter portfolio bets. Expect interesting problems: How do we win activation in a user's first 60 seconds? When should two trial flows become one? How do we expose enough value to convert without giving away the platform? How do we price a credit so that customers consume

The role

You will be the hands-on operator behind our Workday work and a key resolver for our core recruiting systems. Workday testing and implementation

- Handle support tickets and requests with consistent quality and response times.

Continuous improvement

- Track recurring issues and questions, identify root causes, and recommend changes to configuration, process, or training.

- Partner with the enablement team so recurring questions become better training and guidance.

- Help define process around outcomes and actual tool usage, so the tools get used correctly and consistently.

How the role evolves

Early on, your time is split between Workday testing and implementation and core systems resolution. GenAI Acceleration & Architectural Advocacy

Nice-to-Have Skills
