title: HR Enablement Lead
description:
Headquarters: United States, Remote

Job Title: HR Enablement Lead 

Job Location: United States, Remote 

This is a fully remote opportunity and can be worked from any location in the United States. 

ABOUT THE COMPANY: 

Salesloft is building the next era of enterprise revenue — one where teams make confident decisions powered by AI and real signals. By combining our scale, insights, and AI innovation, we're building the industry's first Predictive Revenue System, enabling humans and AI to work together to make smarter decisions and drive consistent growth.

With thousands of customers using our platforms every day, we have an unmatched view into how revenue is actually won — the Revenue Context that reveals what happens, when, and with what outcome. This gives us a unique opportunity to transform an entire category and set a new benchmark for how modern revenue teams operate.

Join us to help transform how companies around the world run revenue — and build the platform that will guide leading revenue teams into the future.

THE OPPORTUNITY: 

At Salesloft, as our HR Enablement Lead, you will be a pivotal member of our high-performing People team. Reporting to [manager, confirm], you will own the creation of learning programs and lead high-impact enablement workshops from beginning to end, and you will help build a cohesive, seamless learning journey for our global workforce. You'll have designated programs that you own end to end, from conception through execution, with hands-on support from leadership as the team builds out its capabilities together.

You'll work closely with our People Business Partners, our Associate People Business Partner, and an L&D coordinator who supports the learning platform and content production. Together you will ramp front-line managers faster, equip the People team with the playbooks and training it needs, and make learning part of how the business runs. This role moves beyond administrative operations to focus on strategic partnership and the integration of AI to empower our people.

On a day-to-day basis, you will:

- Own program lifecycles. Oversee end-to-end program lifecycles, including planning, development, delivery, and assessment.

- Create and lead workshops. Design and facilitate creative, robust enablement workshops and learning solutions for employees at all levels.

- Partner with People Business Partners. Work directly with People Business Partners to identify and align on specific talent gaps, and build solutions that fit what each business needs.

- Ramp front-line managers. Build and run manager and leadership programs, working with the PBPs, so new and developing managers can coach, handle performance conversations, and lead with confidence.

- Own onboarding and new-hire enablement. Create a consistent, practical onboarding experience that gets new employees productive faster.

- Enable the People team. Build playbooks, training and job aids for PBPs and Shared Services on topics such as calibration, employee relations and change management.

- Shape the learning architecture. Help architect a system of learning that is cohesive and provides a seamless journey for employees at all levels.

- Innovate with AI. Experiment with and implement AI-powered tools to automate workflows, personalize curriculum creation, and continuously invest in AI for workforce enablement.

- Drive business execution. Develop tailored strategies to address performance gaps, with clear objectives, development plans, and accountability measures, and make sure all programming aligns with near-term and long-term goals.

- Run the learning platform. Own the LMS and content library, working with the L&D coordinator on administration, scheduling and production.

- Analyze and interpret. Use data to identify trends, monitor program completions and impact, and provide actionable insights that inform future learning strategy.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR: 

We are seeking a strategic, results-driven partner who moves beyond operations to become a true consultant to the business. You are someone who understands how individual success drives company-wide goals and can build robust learning solutions that reflect the pragmatic needs of a fast-growing organization. You are comfortable embedding with the business and the People team. You build as well as plan: you ship programs, not just roadmaps, and you are equally at home designing a strategy and running the session. You care about proving that what you build works.

THE SKILL SET: 

- 5+ years of combined experience in learning and development, enablement, organizational development, HR, or a related field, ideally in a technology-driven environment.

- Workshop facilitation: Proven ability to lead engaging enablement workshops across a variety of formats (live, in-person, or remote).

- Manager and onboarding programs: Experience designing and delivering manager development and onboarding programs.

- Instructional innovation: Proven ability to experiment with emerging learning technologies, creative modalities, and unconventional approaches that push beyond traditional training while applying adult learning principles.

- Strategic partnership: Skilled at building trust and credibility with senior leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.

- AI and technical aptitude: Experience leveraging AI to automate workflows, analyze insights, or create curriculum; aptitude for maintaining learning technology systems.

- Systems thinking: Strong business acumen to understand how learning initiatives impact the broader organization and culture.

- Program ownership: Strong project management skills with a demonstrated ability to work independently to see a program from concept to delivery.

- Hands-on execution: A track record of shipping programs and learning assets on a deadline, from design through delivery.

- Communication and influence: Effective communication skills to present findings and influence diverse audiences across many company levels.

- Instructional design: Strong foundation in instructional design methodologies and frameworks, with experience developing structured curriculum and learning objectives across diverse subject matters.

- Measurement: Experience measuring program impact and reporting results to leaders.

title: Sr. Data Engineer
description:
Headquarters: Remote

About Carrot: 

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com .

The Opportunity 

Carrot is seeking a Sr. Data Engineer to lead the evolution, reliability, and scalability of our modern data infrastructure across analytics, reporting, and business intelligence. In this role, you will architect, build, and maintain robust, automated data pipelines, orchestrate workflows, integrate diverse data sources, and partner with stakeholders across the business to deliver secure, compliant, high-quality data solutions.

Your work will span the full data lifecycle, from architecting resilient ETL/ELT pipelines and developing real-time and batch data integrations to automating reporting, reducing technical debt, and enabling advanced analytics. Sr. Data Engineers at Carrot are operational stewards and technical mentors, driving improvements in system maturity, cost efficiency, automation, and collaborative practices.

You will join our Data Engineering team, which develops and optimizes scalable data pipelines and cloud infrastructure to enable secure, automated reporting and analytics across Carrot. The team collaborates closely with Business Intelligence, Product, Finance, Legal, and Commercial partners to deliver reliable integrations and self-serve solutions that drive business insights and operational efficiency.

What You’ll Own 

In this role, you will:

- Architect, build, test, deploy, and maintain scalable, automated ETL/ELT pipelines using Python, dbt, and orchestration tools such as Prefect and Airflow

- Administer and optimize cloud-based data warehouse and lake platforms, including Snowflake, AWS (S3, Redshift), and Google Cloud, integrating new sources and tuning for performance and cost

- Orchestrate data workflows with custom scheduling, alerting, dependency management, monitoring, and error resolution

- Design and maintain secure external data flows through SFTP, Files.com, and APIs, with a focus on reliability and compliance

- Automate manual reporting and operational tasks, building robust, reusable pipeline components that reduce operational overhead

- Partner with backend product engineers to optimize production database schemas with analytics use cases in mind

- Strengthen data quality, lineage, governance, and documentation practices across key data domains

- Mentor teammates and reinforce best practices in version control, code review, and structured workflow management

What Success Looks Like 

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:

- Taken end-to-end ownership of core pipelines and integrations, with measurable improvements in reliability, data recency, and cost efficiency

- Automated high-effort manual workflows, reducing operational risk and freeing capacity for higher-value engineering work

- Delivered secure, compliant data integrations that stakeholders across the business trust for decision-making

- Strengthened observability across the platform, including monitoring, alerting, and incident response for critical data workflows

- Established yourself as a technical mentor and a go-to partner for Business Intelligence, Product, and cross-functional teams

About You 

You likely have:

- Expert-level proficiency in Snowflake, dbt, and Python for data modeling, transformation, pipeline development, and advanced analytics

- Advanced SQL skills for complex querying, large-scale data model design, and database optimization

- Proven experience architecting, building, testing, deploying, and maintaining scalable, automated ETL/ELT pipelines using modern orchestration tools such as Prefect and Airflow

- Hands-on administration of cloud-based data warehouse and lake platforms, including Snowflake, AWS (S3, Redshift), and Google Cloud

- A strong understanding of secure external data flows through SFTP, Files.com, and APIs, with a focus on reliability and compliance

- Mastery of version control (Git, GitHub) and structured workflow management (Jira) for code review, audit trails, and operational transparency

- A demonstrated ability to automate and simplify complex manual tasks, building robust, reusable pipeline components

- Dependability, adaptability, and a collaborative approach to engineering, thriving in dynamic and ambiguous environments

Nice to Have ⭐ 

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

- Hands-on experience in startup or rapid-growth environments, delivering technical solutions under shifting priorities

- A background supporting business intelligence, analytics, and data science teams through large-scale integrations and multi-tenant reporting

- Familiarity with both batch and event-driven ingestion paradigms, including near-real-time pipelines built on Snowflake, dbt, and Python

- Experience automating operational, financial, or compliance-driven workflows within cloud data environments

- Exposure to audit, privacy, and compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, HIPAA, GDPR, ISO, and SOX, particularly in data governance and secure access controls

- Experience in regulated industries such as healthcare, healthtech, or SaaS

Why This Role Matters 

Reliable data is the foundation of how Carrot operates, from the analytics that guide business decisions to the reporting our customers and partners depend on. The systems this role owns determine the accuracy, recency, and security of data used across the entire company.

As Carrot scales globally, the Sr. Data Engineer will make our data platform more automated, resilient, and cost-efficient, enabling teams across the business to move faster with data they trust. This work directly supports Carrot's mission of expanding access to fertility and family-building care worldwide.

Interview Process 

We believe in a thoughtful and transparent interview process designed to create alignment for both candidates and our team.

For this role, candidates can expect:

- Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes

- Hiring Manager Interview — 30–45 minutes

- Cross-Functional Panel Interviews — 45 minutes

- Executive Leadership Conversation — 30 minutes

- Hiring Manager Wrap-Up — 15 minutes

Throughout the process, we will share additional context about the team, business priorities, customer landscape, and what success looks like in this role.

Why Candidates Join Carrot 

Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.

Highlights include:

- A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.

- A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.

- Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.

- Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.

- Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.

- A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.

- The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

Compensation: 

Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their life inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package. The starting base salary for this position will range from $145,000-$165,000. Actual compensation may vary from posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience. 

Fraud and Security Notice: Please note that all communication regarding job opportunities at Carrot will come exclusively from an @get-carrot.com email address. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them and report the incident to: securityreporting@get-carrot.com 

A Note on AI 

At Carrot, we believe AI can help us work smarter, move faster, and create more meaningful experiences for our members, customers, and each other. While not every role requires deep technical AI expertise, we value people who are curious, eager to learn, and excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI into their day-to-day work.

For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement—and we'll call that out clearly in the qualifications. For everyone else, we're looking for people who embrace new ways of working, use AI responsibly to improve quality and efficiency, and continue to learn as the technology evolves.

Why Carrot? 

Carrot has received national and international recognition for its pioneering work, including Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and World Changing Ideas, Inc. Power Partners, and Modern Healthcare’s Innovators. Carrot’s global workforce has been acknowledged with several accolades, including Fortune’s Best Workplaces in Healthcare, Great Place to Work, and Age-Friendly Employer certifications. Carrot is regularly featured in media reporting on issues related to the future of work, women in leadership, and healthcare innovation, including MSNBC, The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, CNBC, National Public Radio, Harvard Business Review, and more. Learn more at carrotfertility.com. 

To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/carrot-sr-data-engineer

title: Business Intelligence Analyst (Contractor)
description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA or Remote (U.S.)

**This is a contract role expected to last until April 15th, 2027 

Location : This role is Remote in the U.S., with the option to work onsite from our San Francisco, CA headquarters.

Visa sponsorship is not available for this role. 

About Doximity 

Doximity is the leading clinical AI company with the largest network of U.S. clinicians. Doximity’s AI-powered workflow platform is trusted by over 85% of U.S. physicians and 300+ health systems. Doximity's mission is to help clinicians be more productive so they can provide better care for their patients.

At Doximity, we value curiosity, ownership, inclusion, and a commitment to making a meaningful impact. If you're excited about solving complex problems that improve healthcare, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role 

As a Business Intelligence Analyst , you will:

- Work closely with our Product, Strategic Analytics, Client Success, and Sales teams to create client-facing analyses.

- Showcase your engineering skills by creating data products from scratch and automating code so they can be re-used by other teammates.

- Continue to improve your technical and non-technical skill sets.

- Leverage Doximity's extensive datasets to identify and classify behavioral patterns of medical professionals on our platform.

- Grow into a presentation/communication-focused role or dive deeper into more-involved technical challenges—the choice is yours.

What We're Looking For 

We're excited to meet candidates who have many of the following qualifications:

Must have: 

- Three (3) years of experience illustrating collaboration, passion for data, reliability, precision, curiosity, and respect for teammates and clients.

- Excellent SQL skills with proven ability to create and evaluate complex SQL statements involving numerous tables and complex relationships.

- Fluent in Python and experience using common modules (numpy, pandas, statsmodels, matplotlib) for EDA.

- Experience collaborating with non-technical stakeholders.

Nice to have: 

- Working knowledge of statistics and visualization.

- Experience working with data visualization tools.

- Advanced Excel skills.

- Experience using AI coding assistants and building AI-leveraged workflows.

- Experience working in the healthcare industry.

- Experience presenting data to a non-technical audience.

The Core Values of the Client Intelligence team 

As an organization we value diversity - in backgrounds and in experiences. Healthcare is a universal concern, and we need people from all backgrounds to help build a better future for all. Below are additional core values specific to the Insights Team.

- Collaboration —The best candidates and teammates are not only strong in their own aptitudes but care deeply about supporting each other's growth.

- Passion for Data —You’re going to help our clients and team members with data-driven decision making. We need someone that can manipulate millions of rows of data and also ask the right questions to find the important insights.

- Reliability – Our team is efficient, flexible, and agile only because we trust the reliability of each member. We need self-starters and goal-oriented individuals for our continued success.

- Precision – Our team's deliverables power client analysis and inform real-world decisions. A successful candidate will triple check their work and their teammates' work, holding all of us to the highest data quality standards.

- Curiosity – Continuous learning is a cornerstone at Doximity, and curious individuals thrive in our environment. We’re looking for someone who is curious enough about data to go above-and-beyond the task for the true insight.

- Respect – A key dynamic that allows our team to flourish is respect: for ourselves and our quality of work, for our teammates, and for our internal clients who are under the pressure of deadlines and finance goals.

Why You'll Love Working Here 

At Doximity, you'll join a mission-driven company where your work has a meaningful impact on healthcare. We believe great ideas come from empowered teams, and we're committed to creating an environment where people can do their best work.

- Make a real impact. Help build products that support over a million healthcare professionals and ultimately improve patient care.

- Work with exceptional teammates. Collaborate with thoughtful, talented colleagues who value curiosity, humility, and continuous learning.

- Enjoy flexibility and trust. We support flexible ways of working and empower employees with the autonomy to own their work.

- Grow your career. Take on meaningful challenges, develop new skills, and shape your career through mentorship and professional development.

- Bring your authentic self. We're committed to fostering an inclusive culture where diverse perspectives are welcomed, respected, and celebrated.

Our Hiring Process & AI Tools

These tools may assist with administrative tasks such as scheduling, general communication, interview coordination, note-taking, or summarizing interview feedback. title: Director, Category Growth (General Manager)
description:
Headquarters: Remote, USA

Help empower our global customers to connect to culture through their passions. 

Why you’ll love this role: 

StockX has redefined the global marketplace for culture — where buyers and sellers transact with confidence on an always-on digital exchange. We are building the next frontier of creator-driven, culturally rich commerce that blends excitement, community, expertise, and transaction in one platform.

To power this next chapter, we are building a category-led organization where each major vertical operates with clear ownership, accountability, and cultural authority.

The Director, Category Growth (General Manager) is the business owner of a major category vertical. This leader is accountable for the full P&L and long-term trajectory of their category — including supply growth, liquidity, demand activation, monetization, and marketplace health.

You will operate as a true GM: setting vision, defining strategy, allocating resources, building a team, and driving cross-functional execution. You will represent your vertical at the leadership level and ensure that product, marketing, operations, and partnerships are aligned to unlock sustainable growth.

This role is both entrepreneurial and executive — suited for a leader who wants to build and scale a culturally driven business within a high-impact marketplace.

What you’ll own: 

Full-Stack Category P&L 

- Own revenue, contribution margin, liquidity, and growth targets for your vertical

- Develop annual and multi-year business plans, forecasts, and investment cases

- Allocate resources across acquisition, retention, and engagement to maximize ROI

- Drive pricing, incentives, and promotional strategies aligned to marketplace health

Vertical Strategy & Market Leadership 

- Define the long-term category vision, positioning, and competitive differentiation

- Identify expansion opportunities across adjacent segments, geographies, and seller tiers

- Establish scalable supply acquisition and retention strategies

- Continuously assess competitive dynamics and evolving cultural trends

Supply, Demand & Liquidity Engine 

- Architect the playbook for acquiring, activating, and retaining high-value sellers and creators

- Ensure balanced marketplace dynamics between supply depth and demand velocity

- Partner with Growth and Marketing to stimulate demand moments and category engagement

- Implement structural improvements that increase conversion, retention, and monetization

Cross-Functional Executive Leadership 

- Influence Product roadmap to improve seller tooling, pricing mechanics, discovery, and trust features

- Partner with Marketing to launch culturally relevant campaigns and high-impact moments

- Collaborate with Operations to optimize onboarding, seller support, and fulfillment performance

- Represent your vertical in executive planning, QBRs, and strategic reviews

Team & Organizational Build-Out 

- Hire and develop Category Managers and supporting roles as the vertical scales

- Establish operating cadence, reporting frameworks, and performance management systems

- Build repeatable GTM playbooks that can be deployed across additional categories

- Foster a culture of accountability, experimentation, and community authenticity

Ecosystem & Community Stewardship 

- Act as the senior face of StockX within your category’s ecosystem

- Build relationships with top sellers, shops, creators, and community leaders

- Ensure platform growth remains culturally credible and aligned with community norms

About you: 

- 10+ years of experience in marketplace leadership, category general management, business development, or growth roles within consumer tech or two-sided platforms

- Demonstrated ownership of revenue or P&L-level outcomes

- Proven track record of scaling a vertical, marketplace segment, or new business line

- Strong executive presence and experience influencing cross-functional roadmaps

- Deep fluency in marketplace mechanics: liquidity, take rate, CAC/LTV, cohort behavior, supply elasticity

- Experienced people leader with a track record of building high-performing teams

- Deep connection to culture-driven or enthusiast categories

Why this role is different: 

This is not a traditional category marketing or merchandising role. This is a vertical GM role with real business ownership.

You will:

- Build and scale a culturally driven marketplace vertical from early-stage to maturity

- Directly influence product, pricing, and growth strategy

- Operate with executive visibility and measurable business accountability

- Create the blueprint for how category-led growth powers the future of StockX

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, and any other state or local hiring regulations, we will consider for employment any qualified applicant, including those with arrest and conviction records, in a manner consistent with the applicable regulation. 

Pursuant to the Colorado Fair Pay Act, the base salary range in Colorado for this position is $160,000 to $200,000, plus opportunities for benefits (e.g., medical, dental), equity and discretionary bonuses. Compensation in other geographies may vary. 

About StockX 

StockX is proud to be a Detroit-based technology leader focused on the large and growing online market for sneakers, apparel, accessories, electronics, collectibles, trading cards, and more. StockX's powerful platform connects buyers and sellers of high-demand consumer goods from around the world using dynamic pricing mechanics. This approach affords access and market visibility powered by real-time data that empowers buyers and sellers to determine and transact based on market value. The StockX platform features hundreds of brands across verticals including Jordan Brand, adidas, Nike, Supreme, BAPE, Off-White, Louis Vuitton, Gucci; collectibles from brands including LEGO, KAWS, Bearbrick, and Pop Mart; and electronics from industry-leading manufacturers Sony, Microsoft, Meta, and Apple. Launched in 2016, StockX employs 1,000 people across offices and verification centers around the world. Learn more at www.stockx.com.

description:

StockX is the world’s leading marketplace for current culture, built at the intersection of commerce, community, and credibility. Trading Cards are foundational to StockX — not just as products, but as artifacts of fandom, nostalgia, speculation, and identity.

We are expanding how Trading Cards culture shows up on StockX through creator-driven, community-oriented commerce experiences that blend storytelling, expertise, and transaction. To do this well, we need category leaders who don’t just understand collectibles — they live inside them.

The Trading Cards Category Manager is the single-threaded owner of collectibles category growth within a new, high-priority commerce initiative. This person is the in-house expert on trading cards and sports cards, — and is responsible for translating that expertise into supply growth, engagement, and GMV.

You will act as:

- The internal authority on the first-hand and second-hand trading cards ecosystem

- The external face of StockX to collectors, breakers, shops, graders, dealers, and community leaders

- The architect of the trading cards go-to-market playbook for this new initiative

This role blends deep cultural fluency, strategic ownership, and hands-on execution. Early on, you will own everything related to trading cards within this initiative. As the category scales, you will grow into a leader overseeing a broader trading cards portfolio and team.

What You’ll Do: 

Own the Collectibles Category End-to-End 

- Define and execute the growth strategy for trading cards within the platform

- Own category-level performance across supply, engagement, and revenue

- Establish quarterly goals, leading indicators, and operating rhythms

Be the Market & Culture Expert 

Maintain deep, current knowledge of trading card culture, including:

- Key sellers, breakers, dealers, shops, graders, creators, and brands

- Sub-segments such as trading cards (sports and TCG), graded sports cards, etc.

- Product drops, set releases, grading cycles, convention moments, and cultural spikes

- Pricing dynamics, liquidity, population reports, grading premiums, and resale economics

Serve as the internal voice of the trading cards community, informing product, marketing, and platform decisions.

Supply & Creator Acquisition 

- Build and own a pipeline of high-impact sellers across trading cards, sports cards, etc.

- Personally recruit and onboard flagship sellers, breakers, comic shops, etc. who set the tone for the platform

- Develop seller strategies that balance credibility, storytelling, and commerce

Commerce Strategy & Category Moments 

- Identify and orchestrate trading card-specific moments, campaigns, and formats that drive engagement and conversion (e.g., major set releases, championship spikes, grading returns, convention cycles)

- Partner with Category Marketing to design culturally authentic activations

- Experiment with new approaches (live breaks, expert drops, themed auctions, etc.) and iterate quickly based on performance and feedback

Cross-Functional Leadership 

- Work closely with Account and Partnerships Managers to scale seller acquisition and support

- Collaborate with Product and Engineering to shape features and tools that matter to collectors (e.g., condition transparency, grading integrations, pricing insights, population data visibility)

- Provide clear, actionable insights from the market to influence roadmap prioritization

Build the Playbook 

- Document learnings, frameworks, and best practices that can be reused across future categories

- Help define what “great” looks like for category ownership at StockX

- Support hiring and onboarding as the trading card category team grows

About You: 

- Deeply embedded in trading card culture — you know the people, platforms, trends, grading standards, and economics, and you’re already plugged into the ecosystem

- 5+ years of experience in category management, partnerships, marketplace growth, brand, dealer, or operator roles within trading cards, sports cards, comics, toys, coins, or adjacent enthusiast ecosystems

- Comfortable owning outcomes, not just strategy — you execute, iterate, and adapt

- Strong relationship builder with credibility among collectors, breakers, shop owners, graders, dealers, and community members

- Data-literate and commercially minded — you understand pricing spreads, grading premiums, liquidity, margin structures, and incentives

- Entrepreneurial, scrappy, and energized by building something from the ground up

Nice to Have: 

- Existing network of card breakers, LCS owners, comic shops, grading submitters, toy dealers, or coin specialists

- Experience buying, selling, grading, or operating within collectibles marketplaces

- Familiarity with grading ecosystems (e.g., card and comic grading workflows, condition standards, population reports)

- Experience with content-driven commerce, live selling, or enthusiast communities

- Experience working cross-functionally with product and engineering teams

- Experience running your own collectibles business, shop, or online storefront

Why This Role Matters: 

Trading Cards will define the early perception and success of this new commerce initiative at StockX. This role sets:

- The cultural and credibility bar for the platform

- The go-to-market blueprint for future enthusiast categories

- StockX’s reputation within trading cards

You will have outsized influence on how StockX expands its leadership from marketplace into deeper cultural engagement within the global trading card ecosystem.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, and any other state or local hiring regulations, we will consider for employment any qualified applicant, including those with arrest and conviction records, in a manner consistent with the applicable regulation.

About StockX 

StockX is proud to be a Detroit-based technology leader focused on the large and growing online market for sneakers, apparel, accessories, electronics, collectibles, trading cards, and more. StockX's powerful platform connects buyers and sellers of high-demand consumer goods from around the world using dynamic pricing mechanics. This approach affords access and market visibility powered by real-time data that empowers buyers and sellers to determine and transact based on market value. The StockX platform features hundreds of brands across verticals including Jordan Brand, adidas, Nike, Supreme, BAPE, Off-White, Louis Vuitton, Gucci; collectibles from brands including LEGO, KAWS, Bearbrick, and Pop Mart; and electronics from industry-leading manufacturers Sony, Microsoft, Meta, and Apple. title: Lead Product Management
description:
Headquarters: Remote

About Carrot: 

Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each member’s life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries – from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide.

Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets — including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review — as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com .

The Opportunity 

Carrot is seeking a Lead, Product Management to help shape and scale one of our core product areas as Carrot's platform continues to grow. In this role, you'll operate as a strategic driver within the Product organization — owning a significant portion of the product roadmap, setting direction for cross-functional initiatives, and raising the bar for product craft across the team.

This is a highly visible, high-impact role for someone who has already demonstrated strong product judgment and is ready to take on greater scope: shaping strategy, mentoring other product managers, and partnering directly with senior leadership on the initiatives that matter most to our members and business.

If you're energized by solving ambiguous, high-stakes problems and want to help define how Carrot builds products at scale, this role is for you!

What You’ll Own 

In this role, you will:

- Own the end-to-end product strategy and roadmap for a key product area, translating company priorities into a clear, prioritized plan of execution

- Lead cross-functional initiatives, aligning Engineering, UX, Clinical, Legal, and Commercial partners around a shared vision and set of goals

- Serve as a thought partner and informal mentor to other Product Managers, helping raise the bar on product process, discovery, and craft across the team

- Make and communicate high-judgment prioritization decisions, balancing member experience, business impact, and technical feasibility

- Partner directly with senior product and cross-functional leadership to shape quarterly and annual product strategy

- Identify and address systemic gaps in process, tooling, or team practices that limit the Product team's effectiveness

- Represent the Product team in executive and cross-functional forums, clearly communicating strategy, trade-offs, and outcomes

What Success Looks Like 

In your first 12–18 months, you will have:

- Delivered a body of work that measurably improved member outcomes, engagement, or business performance within your product area

- Built trusted, effective working relationships with cross-functional leaders across Engineering, UX, Clinical, Legal, and Commercial/Customer Success

- Established yourself as a go-to product thought leader, with other PMs seeking out your input on strategy and process

- Shaped or improved a core product process (discovery, roadmapping, prioritization) that is now used more broadly across the team

- Successfully led at least one significant, ambiguous, cross-functional initiative from concept through launch

About You 

You likely have:

- 5+ years of product management experience, including time at a fast-growing technology company; healthcare or digital health experience is a plus

- A track record of owning complex, cross-functional product initiatives from strategy through execution

- Strong product sense and the ability to balance user needs, business goals, and technical constraints in your decision-making

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence and align both peers and senior leadership

- Experience mentoring or informally guiding less-experienced product managers

Nice to Have ⭐ 

While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring:

- Experience in fertility, family-building, or broader digital health benefits

- Experience partnering with Clinical or Legal teams on regulated or compliance-sensitive products

- Familiarity with AI-enabled product features or workflows

- Experience operating in a fully distributed, remote-first organization

Why This Role Matters 

As Carrot continues to scale, our Product team needs leaders who can operate with both strategic clarity and hands-on execution. This Lead, Product Management role is central to that effort — helping ensure our roadmap reflects the right priorities, our cross-functional partners are aligned, and our product practices scale sustainably as the team grows.

This is an opportunity to have an outsized impact: shaping not just a single product area, but the way Carrot's Product organization operates as it matures.

Interview Process 

We believe in a thoughtful and transparent interview process designed to create alignment for both candidates and our team.

For this role, candidates can expect:

- Recruiter Screen — 30 minutes

- Hiring Manager Interview — 30–45 minutes

- Cross-Functional Panel Interviews — 45 minutes

- Executive Leadership Conversation — 30 minutes

- Hiring Manager Wrap-Up — 15 minutes

Throughout the process, we will share additional context about the team, business priorities, customer landscape, and what success looks like in this role.

Why Candidates Join Carrot 

Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission.

Highlights include:

- A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally.

- A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact.

- Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits.

- Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge.

- Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits.

- A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture.

- The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide.

Compensation: 

Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their life inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package. The starting base salary for this position will range from $168,000-$198,000. Actual compensation may vary from posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience. 

Fraud and Security Notice: Please note that all communication regarding job opportunities at Carrot will come exclusively from an @get-carrot.com email address. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them and report the incident to: securityreporting@get-carrot.com 

A Note on AI 

At Carrot, we believe AI can help us work smarter, move faster, and create more meaningful experiences for our members, customers, and each other. While not every role requires deep technical AI expertise, we value people who are curious, eager to learn, and excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI into their day-to-day work.

For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement—and we'll call that out clearly in the qualifications. For everyone else, we're looking for people who embrace new ways of working, use AI responsibly to improve quality and efficiency, and continue to learn as the technology evolves.

Why Carrot? 

Carrot has received national and international recognition for its pioneering work, including Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and World Changing Ideas, Inc. Power Partners, and Modern Healthcare’s Innovators. Carrot’s global workforce has been acknowledged with several accolades, including Fortune’s Best Workplaces in Healthcare, Great Place to Work, and Age-Friendly Employer certifications. Carrot is regularly featured in media reporting on issues related to the future of work, women in leadership, and healthcare innovation, including MSNBC, The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, CNBC, National Public Radio, Harvard Business Review, and more. Learn more at carrotfertility.com.

title: Senior Staff Data Scientist
description:
Headquarters: Remote

About the Team: 

Netlify’s Data team helps the company understand and improve the full product-led growth journey, from activation and engagement through conversion, retention, and monetization. We partner closely with Product, Engineering, and Growth to uncover opportunities, evaluate investments, and understand what drives customer and business outcomes.

We’re hiring a Senior Staff Data Scientist to deepen how data shapes our product and growth strategy. You’ll develop an end-to-end understanding of the PLG journey, proactively identify opportunities, and turn complex data into hypotheses, experiments, and recommendations that influence where we invest and what we build. This is a highly autonomous role for someone who can move from identifying an important question to shaping the approach, defining success, and driving toward an answer.

What You'll Do: 

- Own the analytical understanding of Netlify’s PLG performance across activation, engagement, conversion, monetization, and retention, identifying opportunities before they become requests

- Partner with Product and Engineering leadership to turn behavioral insights into product bets, defining what to test, how to measure it, and what the results mean

- Lead experimentation from hypothesis through decision, including study design, methodology, success metrics, guardrails, analysis, and recommendations

- Apply statistical rigor where it matters while recognizing when there is enough signal to make a decision and move forward, and help teams develop that same judgment

- Build scalable analytical systems like semantic models, trusted metrics, proactive monitoring, and AI-powered agents that surface opportunities without waiting to be asked

- Use AI to investigate faster, automate recurring analytical work, and test more hypotheses without sacrificing the judgment that makes the output useful

- Identify gaps in measurement, event instrumentation, and metric definitions, and partner with Data and Product Engineering to close them

- Serve as a trusted analytical partner to PLG leadership, using evidence and product judgment to influence investment decisions and roadmap priorities

- Influence product strategy through evidence, product instincts, and a clear point of view, without relying on formal authority to do it

What You'll Bring: 

- 8+ years of experience in product analytics, growth analytics, or data science, with a track record of high ownership and measurable impact on PLG or consumer product outcomes

- Deep understanding of product and growth dynamics across activation, engagement, conversion, monetization, and retention

- Demonstrated ability to turn behavioral data into product hypotheses and carry them from insight through experimentation and measured outcomes

- Deep experimentation expertise: study design, statistical reasoning, causal inference, and the judgment to know when an experiment has told you what you need to know

- Experience building analytical systems such as metrics layers, monitoring frameworks, or semantic models that teams can rely on over time

- An AI-native approach to analysis: you use AI tools actively to accelerate investigation, automate repetitive work, and surface patterns faster

- A track record of influencing senior stakeholders and product direction through analytical reasoning, clear recommendations, and sound judgment

- Comfort operating with significant autonomy in ambiguous problem spaces, including determining which questions are most important to answer

- Strong written and verbal communication skills in distributed environments, with the ability to make complex findings clear and recommendations actionable

This Role is a Great Fit If: 

- You're energized by finding the opportunity before anyone thought to ask - proactive discovery is how you naturally work, not a mode you shift into

- You think like a product person who happens to be exceptionally rigorous with data, not a data person who occasionally weighs in on product

- You thrive when the problem isn't handed to you - you'd rather define the question worth asking than answer the one that landed in your queue

- You get excited about building systems that keep working after you've moved on to the next problem

- You're comfortable making a call with imperfect information and can articulate clearly why you made it

- You enjoy being a thought partner to senior leaders - shaping how they think about investment and opportunity, not just supporting decisions already made

- You work well in a remote-first, async environment where written clarity and self-direction matter more than proximity

- You're drawn to roles where the measure of success is outcomes, decisions made, bets tested, metrics moved, not volume of output produced

Applying 

Not sure you meet 100% of our qualifications? Please apply anyway! 

When applying please include: 

A resume or short listing of your job history & skills (link to a LinkedIn profile would be fine). We appreciate a cover letter explaining why you would enjoy working in this role at Netlify to get to know you a bit better, though this is not required and will not impact your application. Our mission is to “build a better web” and that cannot be done without a diversity of skill sets, backgrounds and thoughts. 

Of everything we've ever built at Netlify, we are most proud of our team. Netlify is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are devoted to building a team of people with diverse backgrounds and lifestyles. Driving equality empowers our team, enables us to innovate, and helps us maintain a more inclusive environment. We don’t discriminate against employees or applicants based on gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, religion, age, race, military/veteran status, citizenship, pregnancy status, or any other differences. If we can do anything to provide a better interview, i.e. accommodate a disability, then please let us know by emailing accommodations@netlify.com . 

About Netlify 

Netlify is the most popular way to build, deploy, and scale modern web applications, empowering everyone from fast moving solo developers to enterprise teams. Millions of developers and organizations rely on Netlify as their platform of choice for composing web applications that are production ready, performant, and flexible. title: Business Continuity Management Lead
description:
Headquarters: San Francisco, CA, New York, NY, Portland, OR, or Remote within Canada or United States

About the Role 

Mercury is seeking a Business Continuity Management (BCM) Lead to build and lead an enterprise-wide continuity program as we prepare to become a bank. As part of the Risk team, this leader will establish practical standards, clear accountability, and tested capabilities to maintain critical services and recover effectively from disruptions, with direct visibility to the CRO and senior leadership.

This role fills the need for a dedicated leader to coordinate BCM across the organization. The ideal candidate combines deep continuity and resilience expertise with the judgment to build a proportionate program in a fast-moving environment, working effectively with Engineering, Operations, Product, Information Security, Legal, Compliance, and business teams.

The BCM Lead will own the enterprise framework, coordination, oversight, and reporting. Business and technology owners will remain accountable for their continuity plans and recovery execution.Because this is a new program, the Lead will be hands-on in the initial build: facilitating the first round of BIAs and plans side by side with owners, running exercises, and driving identified gaps through remediation. This leader will also work closely with Engineering on technology disaster recovery and with relevant teams on incident response, crisis management, and third-party resilience.

Key Responsibilities 

- Develop and implement Mercury’s enterprise BCM framework, policies, standards, governance, and operating model, with a prioritized implementation roadmap aligned to bank-launch readiness and critical services.

- Partner with business owners to identify critical services, conduct business impact analyses (customer, financial, operational, and regulatory), and map dependencies across people, processes, technology, facilities, and third parties, including single points of failure.

- Establish recovery time objectives (RTOs) and recovery point objectives (RPOs), where applicable, with business and technology owners; challenge gaps between objectives and recovery capabilities.

- Set standards for continuity plans and recovery procedures, and facilitate and support accountable owners in developing actionable plans and alternative operating arrangements.

- Coordinate business continuity with technology disaster recovery, incident response, and crisis management, with clear activation criteria, escalation paths, and communications responsibilities.

- Design and lead a risk-based exercise program, from tabletop simulations to end-to-end recovery tests, and drive lessons learned, remediation tracking, and verification that gaps are closed.

- Partner with Third-Party Risk Management and vendor owners to assess critical provider recovery capabilities, contingency arrangements, and concentration dependencies.

- Embed continuity considerations into new products, material business changes, and technology implementations.

- Establish metrics and reporting that give management and relevant committees visibility into readiness, testing outcomes, material gaps, and overdue remediation.

- Build and lead a growing BCM team, including hiring and developing analysts as the program scales over the next year.

- Deliver role-based training and promote awareness of continuity responsibilities across the organization.

- Support regulatory examinations and bank-launch readiness reviews with accurate documentation and evidence of recovery capability.

Qualifications 

- 10+ years of experience in business continuity management, operational resilience, disaster recovery, or a related discipline within a fintech, financial institution, technology company, or other highly regulated environment.

- Demonstrated experience building or materially enhancing an enterprise BCM program, including governance, implementation, testing, and reporting.

- Strong skills in business impact analysis, critical-service identification, dependency mapping, and recovery objective development.

- Experience developing actionable continuity plans and leading exercises that test recovery assumptions and expose gaps.

- Sufficient technical fluency to work with Engineering on cloud services, system dependencies, data recovery, and technology disaster recovery.

- Working knowledge of third-party risk management, including assessing critical vendor recovery capabilities, contingency arrangements and concentration risk.

- Proven ability to drive cross-functional remediation through influence, with a clear view of where BCM oversight ends and business or technology ownership begins.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain readiness gaps and tradeoffs to senior leadership.

- Experience managing a team of Business Continuity analysts.

Preferred Qualifications 

- Familiarity with banking supervisory expectations for business continuity, and operational resilience.

- Experience operating in a company-building or bank-building environment.

- Familiarity with recognized continuity standards, such as ISO 22301, and BCM tools for plan management, exercises, and issue tracking.

- Relevant professional certification, such as CBCP or MBCI.

Leadership Attributes 

- Pragmatic, first-principles builder who turns ambiguous needs into clear priorities and designs a program that fits Mercury’s operations and scale.

- Takes ownership and follows through from identified gaps to demonstrated recovery.

- Collaborative, low-ego, and effective across the three lines of defense.

- Calm under pressure and able to facilitate clear decisions during disruptions.

- Able to challenge constructively, distinguish material gaps from theoretical concerns, and avoid over-engineering.

*Mercury is a fintech company, not an FDIC-insured bank. Banking services provided through Choice Financial Group and Column N.A., Members FDIC.

description:

About the Role:

Maven is looking for a Head of Member Growth to own one of the most important numbers in the company: enrollments. This role is directly accountable for driving member enrollment into Maven's programs across our core business — and, by extension, the revenue those enrollments generate. You will own the enrollment engine end to end, from awareness through activation, turning eligible lives into engaged members.

Enrollment is not a single-team problem. It sits at the intersection of nearly every function at Maven, and this role is built for someone who thrives there. You'll partner daily with Client Success (who own the client relationships that unlock eligible populations), Marketing (member acquisition and lifecycle), Product (enrollment experience and funnel), Finance (targets, forecasting, and unit economics), Data (measurement, segmentation, and attribution), and Clinical and Operations teams. Because so many teams touch enrollment, a core part of the job is holding those cross-functional partners accountable to their piece of the machine — the engine only works when every team delivers its part.

This is a player-coach role. You will lead a small, high-caliber team while remaining deeply hands-on yourself every day. Although it carries a Senior Director title, it is explicitly NOT a leaned-out management position for someone who wants to direct a team from a distance. This is a hard requirement: the person in this seat reads the data themselves, pressure-tests the funnel, drafts the plan, and does the work alongside the team. We are looking for a builder and operator who also develops people — not a manager who has stepped away from the work.

We're also looking for someone who can expand the definition of the job. A great deal of enrollment optimization work is already underway, but there is not enough strategic thinking about fundamentally new ways to drive enrollments — approaches that don't simply depend on securing permission to communicate with a client's employees. This role is expected to find and open those new avenues, not just optimize the existing ones.

What You'll Do:

- Own member growth for the Core Business: Be directly accountable for enrollment targets across Maven's core business and for the revenue those enrollments drive. Set the strategy, build the plan, and act as a control tower across all cross-functional teams driving revenue to deliver the results quarter over quarter.

- Build and run a scalable enrollment engine : Own the full journey from eligible population to enrolled, activated member — spanning client launches, member acquisition and messaging, the enrollment product experience, and re-engagement of eligible-but-not-enrolled members.

- Expand the playbook and deliver new strategies to drive sustainable member growth : Think strategically and from first principles about new ways to grow enrollments beyond today's optimization work — including partnerships and approaches that don't rely solely on permission to communicate with a client's employees. Identify, size, and open avenues that expand the team's purview and unlock new growth. 

- Optimize relentlessly around data : Build and consistently iterate on the funnel, and create systems that enable quick diagnoses of opportunities. Build operational metrics that act as leading KPIs for each team contributing to enrollments and bring quantitative rigor into how teams execute against targets.

- Hold the cross-functional machine accountable : Partner daily with Client Success, Marketing, Product, Finance, Data, Clinical, Payer, Sales, and Operations — and hold each team accountable to its operational KPIs in the enrollment process. Serve as the connective tissue that keeps every part of the engine delivering.

- Operate as a player-coach : Lead and develop a small, high-performing team while staying in the execution and details. Set the bar for rigor and hands-on execution by doing the work, coaching through it, and multiplying the team's impact rather than stepping back from it. This is a role that comes with an expectation that you directly execute on the work.

- Instrument and forecast : Partner with Data and Finance to build the measurement, segmentation, attribution, and forecasting needed to know exactly what is and isn't working, and to forecast enrollment and revenue with confidence.

What You'll Bring:

- 10+ years of experience driving growth, enrollment, acquisition, or revenue outcomes, with a track record of personally owning and hitting a number — ideally in healthcare, benefits, marketplaces, consumer subscription, or another environment with a complex funnel and multiple stakeholders.

- A hands-on player-coach. You are energized by being in the details daily — the data, the funnel, the plan, the execution — and you lead a small team as a way to multiply your own hands-on impact, not to step back from the work. This is a hard requirement for the role. 

- Elite quantitative ability as a core competency. You can build and interrogate a funnel model yourself, size opportunities, design experiments, and instinctively optimize around data rather than intuition. Strong quant is non-negotiable.

- Strategic range. Beyond optimizing what exists, you can spot and pursue fundamentally new approaches to enrollment that expand the team's purview — not just incremental improvements to current channels.

- Cross-functional leadership and accountability. Proven ability to align and mobilize many teams — Client Success, Marketing, Product, Finance, Data, Clinical, Operations — around a shared goal without direct authority over most of them, and to hold each accountable to its operational commitments.

- Commercial instincts. You understand how enrollment translates into revenue and unit economics, and you can partner with Finance on targets and forecasting.

- Comfort in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment with high visibility and direct accountability for a top-line company metric.

The base salary range for this role is $204,000.00 - $270,000.00 per year. You will also be entitled to receive bonus, equity, and benefits. Individual pay decisions are based on qualifications, experience, and skillset.

This role requires active work authorization in the US. 

Maven embraces a flexible hybrid work model. Our teams primarily operate from the New York Metropolitan area, NY, and remotely via San Francisco/Bay Area, CA, Seattle, WA. For those in our New York City office, we encourage in-person collaboration by requiring team members to work onsite three days a week (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday). For those based in Boston, DC, Chicago, Seattle, and San Francisco, we encourage in-person collaboration by requiring team members to attend monthly Work Together Days within these cities. This policy aims to balance remote work flexibility with the benefits of face-to-face interaction.

At Maven we believe that a diverse set of backgrounds and experiences enrich our teams and allow us to achieve above and beyond our goals. If you do not have experience in all of the areas detailed above, we hope that you will share your unique background with us in your application and how it can be additive to our teams.

Benefits That Work For You 

Our benefits are designed to support your health, well-being and career development, helping you thrive both personally and professionally. We remain focused on providing a competitive benefits package for our employees. On top of standards such as employer-covered health, dental, and insurance plan options, we offer an inclusive approach to benefits:

As a Sr. Data Engineer at Oportun, you will be a key member of our team, responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining sophisticated software / data platforms in achieving the charter of the engineering group. Your mastery of a technical domain enables you to take up business problems and solve them with a technical solution. With your depth of expertise and leadership abilities, you will actively contribute to architectural decisions, mentor junior engineers, and collaborate closely with cross-functional teams to deliver high-quality, scalable software solutions that advance our impact in the market. This is a role where you will have the opportunity to take up responsibility in leading the technology effort – from technical requirements gathering to final successful delivery of the product - for large initiatives (cross-functional and multi-month-long projects). 

At Oportun, we move fast and we hold each other to a high bar. If you care about doing your best work while actually moving the needle for real people, you'll fit right in. 

What You'll Do 

Your day-to-day 

- You’ll design and implement scalable, efficient, and reliable data architectures that support business and analytical needs. 

- You’ll build and maintain data pipelines, ETL processes, and integration solutions for large volumes of structured and unstructured data. 

- You’ll optimize data pipelines, databases, data warehouses, and data lakes for performance, reliability, scalability, and security. 

- You’ll partner with stakeholders to understand data requirements, develop domain expertise, and translate business needs into effective data models and solutions. 

- You’ll establish and improve data quality standards, validation rules, documentation, and governance practices. 

- You’ll implement monitoring and observability practices to identify bottlenecks, improve performance, and strengthen platform reliability. 

- You’ll provide technical leadership on architecture, scalability, reliability, monitoring, integration, and extensibility. 

- You’ll lead and contribute to code reviews, helping maintain high standards for code quality, performance, and maintainability. 

- You’ll mentor junior engineers and support a culture of continuous learning and technical excellence. 

- You’ll take ownership of production issues, including troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, escalation, and long-term resolution. 

- You’ll independently lead multiple features and projects, coordinate work across engineers, and keep stakeholders informed of progress, risks, and dependencies. 

- You’ll help evolve engineering tools, platforms, and practices and encourage adoption of better ways of working. 

- You’ll look for practical ways to use AI tools to improve engineering productivity, analysis, documentation, and problem-solving. 

Who You Are 

The right fit looks like this 

You’re a hands-on data engineer who enjoys solving complex technical problems and building systems that others depend on. You combine strong technical depth with a practical understanding of business needs and know how to turn ambiguous requirements into scalable solutions. 

You take ownership, communicate clearly, and are comfortable leading technical work without relying on formal authority. You enjoy mentoring others and helping teams make stronger technical decisions. 

What You Bring 

Skills & experience 

Required 

- 8+ years of experience in data engineering, with strong experience in data architecture, ETL, and database management. 

- Strong programming skills in Python or PySpark, plus experience with Java or Scala. 

- Experience building complex end-to-end data pipelines and data integration solutions. 

- Strong knowledge of SQL and experience with relational and NoSQL database technologies. 

- Experience with big data technologies such as Spark, Kafka, Hadoop, or similar platforms. 

- Experience with orchestration and scheduling tools such as Airflow, Databricks, Jenkins, or similar technologies. 

- Experience designing and operating scalable, reliable, and secure data systems. 

- Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP and associated data services. 

- Experience working in Agile environments such as Scrum, Lean, or Kanban. 

- Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills. 

- Experience mentoring junior engineers and contributing to technical leadership within a team. 

- Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work effectively across technical and non-technical teams. 

Nice to Have 

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Data Science, or a related field.

- Databricks experience or certification.

- Experience with AWS Redshift, S3, Azure SQL Data Warehouse, or comparable cloud data services.

- Experience implementing data governance, data quality, or observability frameworks.

- Experience leading cross-functional or multi-month engineering initiatives.

- Experience using AI-assisted engineering tools to improve development, troubleshooting, documentation, or productivity.

Our AI Mindset 

We build with AI. We lead with judgment. 

AI isn't a feature here. It's how we work. 

We're excited about what AI makes possible, and we're looking for people who share that curiosity. You don't need to be an expert. You need to be open to experimenting , willing to learn, and able to apply new tools in ways that actually move the needle. 

In this role, you'll be encouraged to explore AI tools, find practical use cases for your function, and bring ideas for working smarter. We believe the best outcomes come when human judgment and AI capability work together.

title: Client Value Partner (CVP) - Utilities & Energy Industry
description:
Headquarters: Remote, US, Ohio

Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI. At our core is the Celonis Context Model — which combines process data, business knowledge, and intelligence into a living digital twin of the enterprise that AI can actually understand, turning AI's operational blind spots into operational clarity. World's leading companies trust Celonis and its global ecosystem of partners to make their AI agents, people, systems, and processes work together, achieving transformational outcomes. We believe there's a massive opportunity to unlock global productivity and sustainability by giving AI the context to understand how every business process really works. Join our mission to make processes work for people, companies, and the planet.

The Opportunity 

We are seeking an established consulting leader—a current Big Four Director, Managing Director, or Partner-track Senior Manager—to spearhead our highest-stakes Energy & Utilities engagements. In this executive-level role, you will serve as the principal strategic architect for our most valuable power, gas, and renewable energy accounts globally.

Leveraging the Celonis Process Intelligence platform, you will bridge the gap between macro energy sector strategies and modern cloud/AI execution models, moving clients from slide decks to realized operational value.

The Impact You’ll Make 

1. C-Suite Advisory & Value Architecture 

- Peer-to-Peer Advisory: Partner directly with utility C-suite executives (CEOs, COOs, CFOs, Chief Sustainability Officers) to align macro pressures—decarbonization, grid modernization, and capital reallocation—with execution-level transformation roadmaps.

- Map Enterprise Digital Twins: Oversee the deployment of the Celonis Process Intelligence Graph to build systemic, end-to-end operational models of complex utility enterprises.

- Orchestrate $100M+ Business Cases: Direct the formulation of board-ready Celonis Value Assessments, delivering the economic justification, working capital improvements, and OPEX returns required to greenlight massive cloud and Edge AI investments.

2. Transformation Leadership & Ecosystem Governance 

- Steer Enterprise Transformations: Serve as the executive sponsor for high-visibility, Celonis-driven operating model overhauls for Fortune 500 E&U clients, guiding them from diagnostic discovery to closed-loop automation.

- Architect Celonis Centers of Excellence (CoEs): Design and establish corporate-wide CoEs, defining the target operating models, governance structures, and enablement frameworks needed to embed data-driven decision-making into client cultures.

- Untangle Systemic Friction: Lead cross-functional teams to resolve complex operational leakages where siloed utility stacks (SAP S/4HANA, IBM Maximo, ADMS/SCADA) collide—specifically optimizing capital procurement, field services, and energy settlement invoicing.

3. Commercial Growth & Scaled Innovation 

- De-Risk High-Value Sales Cycles: Convert complex regulatory mandates (FERC, NERC) into automated, visual compliance audits within the Celonis platform, transforming abstract compliance risks into compelling business cases that accelerate C-suite sign-off.

- Commercialize Next-Gen "Process + AI" Use Cases: Direct the integration of industrial telemetry (SCADA, Edge IoT) into Celonis, translating complex data structures into high-margin, executive-ready offerings like real-time storm response and predictive asset failure.

- Productize Utility Value Plays: Codify repeatable client successes into scalable Celonis apps and action templates, establishing a library of industry-specific intellectual property that drives rapid time-to-value, net-new ARR, and account expansion.

The Profile We Are Looking For 

- Consulting Pedigree: 12+ years of progressive experience within a Big Four or elite management consulting firm, currently operating at the Director, Managing Director, or Partner level.

- E&U Vertical Expertise: Deep, authoritative knowledge of the Energy & Utilities sector (Grid Operations, Transmission & Distribution, Generation, or Retail), with a track record of leading multi-million-dollar transformation programs.

- SaaS & Process Intelligence Vision: Strong conceptual understanding of Process Mining paradigms. Experience with Celonis is highly advantageous, but a proven ability to leverage enterprise software to reshape business processes is required.

- Architectural Fluency: Comprehensive understanding of the modern enterprise stack (SAP, Oracle, Maximo) and emerging data/AI paradigms (Azure AI, LLMs). Note: You do not need to write code or SQL queries, but you must possess the technical fluency to direct data scientists, engineers, and solution architects. 

- Commercial Acumen: Proven capability in client origination, relationship management, and driving account growth through value-based selling.

- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or Information Systems. An MBA from a top-tier business school is highly preferred.

Visa sponsorship is not offered for this role. 

What Celonis can offer you: 

- Pioneer Innovation: Work with the global leader in Process Mining and the Process Intelligence Graph to shape the future of AI-driven business operations.

- Ownership from Day 1: Every full-time "Celonaut" is an owner, receiving Restricted Stock Units (RSUs) and merit-based refresh grants.

- Unrivaled Family Support: Benefit from our inclusive parental leave policy—24 weeks of fully paid leave for primary carers and 12 weeks for supporting carers, available from your first day of employment.

- Work-Life Integration: Enjoy Unlimited PTO (in applicable regions) and generous PTO globally, as well as a flexible hybrid work model that balances remote focus with vibrant office collaboration.

- Continuous Growth: Elevate your skills through our 70-20-10 learning framework, mentorship programs, and access to a dedicated learning platform.

- Holistic Well-being: Prioritize your health with subsidized Wellhub memberships, mental health counseling, and dedicated "Wellness Weeks" that prioritize work/life balance.

- Drive Sustainability: Participate in annual Impact Days, where you receive paid time off to volunteer for community and environmental causes with your local office, or virtually.

- Global Inclusion & Belonging: Find community through our Inclusion Think Tank and participate in our annual Inclusion Days, ensuring every voice is heard and valued.

- Value-Driven Impact: Join a mission-led organization where our core values—Live for Customer Value, The Best Team Wins, We Own It, and Earth Is Our Future—drive every decision.

Celonis is the trusted platform to industrialize Enterprise AI, empowering organizations to analyze, design, and operate AI-driven processes. description:

Reddit is a community of communities. It’s built on shared interests, passion, and trust, and is home to the most open and authentic conversations on the internet. Every day, Reddit users submit, vote, and comment on the topics they care most about. With 100,000+ active communities and approximately 130 million daily active unique visitors, Reddit is one of the internet’s largest sources of information. For more information, visit www.redditinc.com .

Your work will empower thousands of your colleagues to improve the user experience and grow our consumer base.

Successful candidates have a strong track record of understanding and deeply caring about the purpose of data to support business goals, and can act as an effective conduit between Data Producers and Data Consumers. - Be a key contributor and collaborator to the success of data quality, performance, reliability, and automation initiatives.

- Manage a portfolio of data products that deliver high-quality, trustworthy data

- Develop and maintain robust data pipelines and workflows for data ingestion, processing, and transformation. Work closely with engineering to ensure the quality and reliability of these data pipelines.

- Create and manage new data integrations across internal and external systems

- Create tools and applications for internal use that streamline data analysis and reporting. Drive widespread adoption of these tools and applications with a relentless focus on automation, consistency, and reliability.

- Serve as a thought partner for data scientists, engineering managers, and leadership on data foundations, communicating and shaping the data foundations roadmap and strategy for Reddit.

- Bachelor's degree in computer science or a quant educational field

- Deep understanding of technical and functional designs for relational and MPP Databases.
